title: A record is one row of its kind's table, with typed columns, and its links are rows of their relations' tables
when: Loads a clean product's data.
then: Expects a use case with its typed columns, its parent, product and domain, and its actor as a part row, a domain rule's statement, an applies link as a row, and no problems.

title: A record points at the code that builds it and the code that proves it (file)
then: Expects a component's and a test's `file` loaded as repo-relative paths, and the test to count towards coverage.

title: A data file's line order and each line's column order do not change what it means, and a file that is not <table>.jsonl is ignored
when: Copies the clean product's data with each file's lines reversed and each line's columns reversed, next to a README.md.
then: Expects the same records, links and coverage, and no problems.

title: Two records with the same ID are refused, even of different kinds or products
when: Loads a domain with an aggregate's ID, in the aggregate's product and in another.
then: Expects the store to refuse each with a `unique-id` problem naming the ID.

title: An ID that does not match the pattern is refused
when: Loads an aggregate with a lower-case ID.
then: Expects the registry's check to refuse it, naming the ID.

title: A missing, unknown, disallowed or looping parent is refused, as is a product with a parent
when: Loads an aggregate with no domain, one naming a domain that does not exist, one naming an aggregate as its domain, two layers inside each other, and a product with a parent.
then: Expects a required-column refusal, foreign-key refusals, a cycle refused as sitting inside itself, and the product's parent refused as a column its table lacks.

title: A record without a title, of an unknown kind or without its kind's required columns is refused
when: Loads an aggregate with no title and one with a blank title, a file for a table that does not exist, and an endpoint with no route.
then: Expects each refused: a missing or blank required column, and an unknown table naming its file.

title: A link to a record that does not exist is refused
when: Loads a use case that applies a missing rule.
then: Expects a foreign-key refusal naming the applies file.

title: A link whose relation is unknown or not allowed for its kinds is refused
when: Loads a link of a relation that has no table, and a view that fulfills a domain rule.
then: Expects an unknown-table refusal and a relation-pair refusal.

title: A test whose file is missing or does not name what it proves is an error; a missing component file is only a warning
when: Loads tests whose files are missing or do not name what they prove, and a component whose file is not written yet.
then: Expects `test-file-missing` and `proof-not-in-file` errors, and only warnings for the component.

title: Coverage counts a rule under an entity and a component in a sub-layer as one level up
then: Expects the coverage of a domain that keeps its rule under an entity and a component in a sub-layer to equal, ID for ID, that of a twin domain that keeps both one level up.

title: Every check reports the deeper domain exactly as the flatter one, apart from its extra layer
then: Expects the twin domains' problems, other than those on layers, to be equal ID for ID, covering file, proof and coverage warnings, and no `rule-not-applied`, `obligation-outside-domain`, `component-outside-layer` or `unsatisfied` problem.

title: Sub-layers of one layer need their own positions; they may reuse the positions of layers elsewhere
then: Expects a `layer-order` error on each of two sub-layers of one layer with the same position, naming the parent layer, and none for a sub-layer that shares a position with a layer elsewhere.

title: A domain whose title names a technology layer, in any letter case, is a warning that says to name the capability
then: Expects `domain-named-for-technology` warnings for domains titled Web App, Payments API, ELECTRON shell and Reporting databases, each naming the word it found and saying to name the capability and make the technology a layer.

title: A domain whose code names a technology is a warning, and one named so in both title and code says both
then: Expects a warning for a domain coded BACKEND under a capability title, and one message naming both the title and the code for a domain titled Front-end and coded FRONTEND.

title: A technology word inside a longer word, or only in the domain's description, is not reported
then: Expects no warning for Building permits, Engineering reviews, or a Lending domain whose description names the web app, API, server and desktop app.

title: A rule under a domain that involves fewer than two aggregates is a warning that says to move a one-aggregate rule onto it; a link to no aggregate is refused
then: Expects `domain-rule-involves` warnings for rules under their domain that involve no aggregate or one, none for rules that involve two or three, and an involves link to a record that is no aggregate refused.

title: A rule under a domain that involves an aggregate of another domain is a warning that says a rule across domains is a domain event's job
then: Expects one `domain-rule-involves` warning for a rule that involves an aggregate of its own domain and one of another, naming that aggregate's domain and saying to raise an event in one domain and react to it in the other.

title: A rule under an aggregate or an entity that uses involves is a warning; one without involves is not
then: Expects one `domain-rule-involves` warning each for a rule under an aggregate and a rule under an entity that use `involves`, none for a rule under an aggregate without it, and only warnings from the check.

title: A domain rule involves aggregates, labeled "Involves" and "Involved in" with no role, and the reference says when
then: Expects the `involves` relation from domain rule to aggregate with its labels and no role, a rule's involves links, the domain rule kind's description saying when, and the check's explanation in the reference.

title: Every rule and requirement in Lathe's own spec states its rule with MUST, SHOULD or MAY under a short title
when: Loads this repo's data.
then: Expects every Lathe requirement and domain rule statement to use MUST, SHOULD or MAY, under a title of at most 15 words.

title: The format page says how records are kept, then shows the kinds by stage and folder, the relations and the checks by severity, as clickable rows
when: Opens `/format`.
then: Expects the title in the pane, the side bar's counts, the section on how records are kept, a kind row under Define, Capabilities leading to its page, the relations by their words, and the checks under Errors and Warnings leading to their pages.

title: A kind page shows where the kind sits, its columns, its links in and out by their labels, its checks, an example and its records
when: Opens the use case kind's page.
then: Expects its description, stage and folder, parent link, each column with its type, requirement and anchor, the ID convention and obligation, links out and in by their labels, the checks that concern it, an example record and its records by parent.

title: A check page shows its severity, explanation and query, and its problems now as clickable rows
when: Opens a check's page.
then: Expects its summary, rendered explanation, query and its problems as clickable rows, with the side bar's facts; a check that reports nothing says so, and an unknown check or kind says it is not in the format.

title: The side bar's kind, each problem code and each column label link to their format pages
when: Opens a record page, a domain page, the Checks page and a group page.
then: Expects the Kind row and a column label to link to the kind's page and its column, each problem code to its check's page, and a group's kind to its page.

title: The record format is a palette command and a link in the shortcuts sheet, not a nav footer link
then: Expects no Record format link in the nav, follows the link in the shortcuts sheet to `/format`, and finds the Record format command in the palette.

title: Quick find finds kinds and checks by name and leads to their pages
when: Ranks "Kind: Use case" and a check by its name, and a check a problem names before the reference loads; then types in quick find and opens a check's page with Enter.

title: The pages are built from the loaded data: a check with no row in the check table is the engine's own, listed without an explanation
when: Opens `/format` and an engine problem's check page.
then: Expects only GET /api/spec requested, the engine's check listed, and its page saying the engine reports it itself, with its problems.

title: Format addresses parse to their pages
when: Parses `/format`, a kind's address, a check's address and an unknown one.

title: The record actions take only a known action and a record ID, and find the data file themselves
when: Accepts each action with a record ID.
then: Refuses paths, unknown actions, lower-case and malformed IDs and extra keys; finds the data file whose row starts with the record's ID, never one that only names it, and again after it changes; and builds the native menu.

title: Open in editor uses VS Code by default, another known editor, the default app or a command of one's own
when: Reads settings with VS Code as the fallback, opens known editors by bundle ID on macOS and by command elsewhere, passes the file to a custom command as an argument and never in its text, and names the editor for the menu.

title: The reference says what a domain is: one business capability, never a technology layer, with the check that holds it
when: Builds the reference.
then: Expects the domain kind's description to call a domain one business capability, never a technology layer, and the `domain-named-for-technology` check's explanation to call it a vertical slice whose technology is a layer inside its Design stage, linked from the kind's entry.

title: In the desktop app a record offers its file actions and a native menu, the page reports its errors, and full screen drops the traffic lights' room
when: Opens a record in a browser, then in the desktop app.
then: Expects no record actions in a browser; in the desktop app, Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID for the record's data file; a right-click on the page title or a record link asking for the native menu, and elsewhere the page's own; the error count sent for the Dock badge; the title bar's room following full screen; and records found under nodes, links and titles.

title: A record's text naming another product's record is plain text: products are separate spaces
when: Loads two products, where a use case's text names a record of the other product.
then: Expects the text kept, no link from the use case, and no problem about the other product's ID.

title: A standard and its rules sit in Shared under the product, and components and tests meet a rule
when: Loads the standards fixture.
then: Expects the `standard` and `standard_rule` kinds in Shared right after the pattern rule, not obligations, the three `meets` pairs labeled Meets and Met by with no role, and a meets from a requirement or to a missing rule refused.

title: A standard rule is never owed, and an ID named in a description is plain text, not a link
then: Expects no standard rule in the domain's coverage or gaps, and a component whose description names a rule to have no meets link and no problem about it.

title: A standard rule that nothing meets is a warning; naming it in text does not meet it
then: Expects `standard-rule-unmet` warnings for exactly the rules no record meets, those only named in text included, each naming the meets link to add.

title: The product lists its standards under Shared, beside its patterns
when: Opens the product.
then: Expects one Shared folder counting the pattern and the standard, listing the pattern then the standard, and no standard among the product's groups.

title: A standard's page lists its rules with what meets each one
when: Opens a standard.
then: Expects its Rules table with the columns Rule and Met by, a met rule's row linking the component and the test that meet it, and Nothing yet for a rule nothing meets.

title: A standard rule's Traceability shows Met by, and what meets it shows Meets
when: Opens a standard rule.
then: Expects Met by in its Traceability with the component and the test and no gaps; then opens the component and expects the rule under Meets.

title: The format reference has a page for each standard kind, from the schema
when: Opens the standard rule's kind page.
then: Expects its folder, Shared, its parent kind, standard, Met by among its links in, from a component, and its description.

title: The graph draws a standard as a pattern with a ruler in Shared and meets as a design line in its key
then: Expects the standard under its product's Shared folder with its rules under it, drawn in the Design stage's colors as stacked boxes and its rules as octagons, each with a ruler mark, `meets` in the design line style, and the key's Design, shape, ruler and design line entries naming them.

title: The modeling skill's first step finds the business capabilities and makes each a slice, with the questions that tell one from a layer
when: Reads the `model-a-domain` skill.
then: Expects its first section to find the business capabilities before any record is written, and to ask at least four questions that tell a capability from a layer.

title: An API sits in a domain and holds its endpoints and the interaction requirements they share
when: Loads a domain with an API holding an endpoint and a shared interaction requirement.
then: Expects the `api` kind, `endpoint` widened to sit in an API, the two kinds an API may hold, and no errors.

title: An integration holds one interaction requirement per exchange and may name its system, and an interaction requirement may sit under the domain
then: Expects the `integration` kind with its `system` field kept, an exchange under it, an interaction requirement directly under the domain, all four counted as the domain's interaction requirements, and no parent errors.

title: A technical flow sits in a domain or a layer and deepens a flow, and its steps have a position, use components and satisfy obligations
then: Expects the `design_flow` and `design_step` kinds with their parents and required columns, their seven relation pairs, a step with its position, path, transaction_name, locks and statements, and a step on another path sharing a position with no problem.

title: A technical step's satisfies counts as design, but only a component whose file exists counts as built
then: Expects obligations designed only by technical steps to count as designed and not built, and no `unsatisfied` warning or satisfies gap.

title: A technical step's position is checked on its path, as a flow step's is
then: Expects a position that is not a whole number, a repeated one and a missing one refused, and one `step-order` error worded for a technical step on a path that skips a number.

title: A technical flow that deepens no flow is a design-flow-deepens-nothing warning
then: Expects one `design-flow-deepens-nothing` warning on the technical flow with no deepens, and a technical flow under a flow refused, having no column for it.

title: An applies-when setting the pattern lacks, or an applies-when given in part, is refused by the store
then: Expects a rule that applies when a setting its pattern lacks refused as a foreign key, a condition given in part refused by its check, and the fixture's rules all loaded.

title: A field name is unique in its entity or event trimmed and in any letter case
when: Loads, and writes, entity and event fields named like another of the same record but for spacing or case.
then: Expects each refused, naming the file and line or the command, the same name kept in two entities, and names that differ in more than spacing and case kept.

title: Reads kinds, folders and relations from the schema, kinds in the schema's order
key: kinds in the schema
when: Builds the app's workspace from a product's schema description.
then: Expects kinds in the schema's kind positions, from product, domain and capability to question, and each kind's label, stage, folder, parents and required columns.

title: The migrations are numbered in order and recorded as applied
key: are numbered in order and recorded as applied
when: Applies the migrations to a fresh database.
then: Expects them numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on, each recorded with its name.

title: Duplicate IDs are refused by the store, in one table or across two
when: Loads an aggregate twice, and a view with an aggregate's ID.
then: Expects a primary-key refusal naming the file and ID, and a `unique-id` refusal saying which kind already has the ID.

title: The row types in src/store/tables.ts match the schema
key: matches the generated row types in src/store/tables.ts
when: Renders the row types from the schema description.
then: Expects them to equal the committed `lathe/src/store/tables.ts`.

title: The schema describes every table and every column of a stored table
key: describes every table and every column of a stored table
then: Expects a description on every table, and on every column of a stored table that is not a link table.

title: Every kind has an ID in the registry, a title and its parent columns
key: gives every kind an id in the registry, a title and its parent columns
then: Expects each kind's table keyed by an ID that is a foreign key into the registry, a required title, a foreign key for each parent column, and a required parent column on every kind but product.

title: Each relation's pairs fit its link table's ends
key: pairs to its link table
then: Expects every relation to have pairs, each pair's kinds accepted by the link table's ends or their supertypes, and every supertype member a kind.

title: Data files are the same bytes whatever order the rows were written in
key: are the same bytes whatever order the rows were written in
when: Writes the same rows in two orders, then reloads and rewrites them.
then: Expects the same bytes each time.

title: Data files hold one JSON object per line, sorted by key, columns in table order
key: hold one JSON object per line, sorted by key, columns in table order
then: Expects one object per line, rows sorted by key with numbers as numbers, columns in the table's order, empty columns left out, and a trailing newline.

title: Data files keep text as UTF-8, and a table file goes when its last row goes
key: keep text as UTF-8, and drop a table file when its last row goes
then: Expects text kept as UTF-8, and no file for a table whose last row is removed.

title: An ID another record has, of any kind, is refused
key: refuses an ID another record has, of any kind
then: Expects a record with another kind's ID refused.

title: A line that is not JSON, a column the table lacks and a file for no table are named by file and line
key: names the file and line of a line that is not JSON
then: Expects each refused, naming its file and line.

title: A row without a required field is refused
key: refuses a row without a required field
then: Expects the row refused, naming the column.

title: A link to a missing record is refused by the store
when: Loads a use case that applies a rule no record has.
then: Expects a foreign-key refusal naming the file, the line and the missing ID.

title: The merge keeps the rows both sides added, sorted
key: keeps the rows both sides added, sorted
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects both sides' new rows in the merged file, sorted by key.

title: The merge takes a change or a removal made on one side only
key: takes a change or a removal made on one side only
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects the one side's change and removal in the merged file.

title: The merge keeps one copy of a row both sides added alike, and of a link both sides made
key: keeps one copy of a row both sides added alike
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects each row once.

title: The merge fails when one ID is added on both sides with different content
key: fails when one ID is added on both sides with different content
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects a clash naming the key.

title: The merge fails when one row is changed on both sides, or removed on one and changed on the other

when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.

title: The merge checks the merged table's own rules
key: checks the merged table's own rules
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.

title: lathe merge-data writes the merge over ours, as git expects
key: writes the merge over ours, as git expects
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects the merged file written over ours.

title: lathe merge-data exits 1 with the clash on a real clash, and 0 on a clean merge
key: exits 1 with the clash on a real clash, and 0 on a clean merge
when: Merges a data file's base, ours and theirs.
then: Expects exit 1 naming the clash, and 0 for a clean merge.

title: lathe add adds a record from its column flags and prints the row and the file
key: adds a record from its column flags and prints the row and the file
then: Expects the row added and printed with its file.

title: lathe add gives each table its columns as help, from the schema
key: gives each table its columns as help, from the schema
then: Expects each column with its type and meaning from the schema description.

title: A disallowed relation is refused by the store; a question may be about any record
when: Loads a view that satisfies a requirement, a view that fulfills a domain rule, a relation that has no table, and a question about a view.
then: Expects a foreign-key, a relation-pair and an unknown-table refusal, and the question's `about` link accepted, since `about` targets any record.

title: lathe add refuses a write the command layer refuses, printing the reason, and changes nothing
key: refuses a write the command layer refuses, printing the reason, and changes nothing
then: Expects every reason printed, an exit code of 1 and the data files unchanged.

title: lathe add refuses a flag that is no column, or a value of the wrong type, as bad usage
key: refuses a flag that is no column, or a value of the wrong type, as bad usage
then: Expects bad usage and no write.

title: lathe set changes a record by its ID, and clears a column given empty
key: changes a record by its ID, and clears a column given as
then: Expects the column changed, and the one given empty cleared.

title: lathe move moves a record and reports every row that changed with it
key: moves a record and reports every row that changed with it
then: Expects the record under its new parent, and every row that moved with it reported.

title: lathe link and unlink link and unlink two records
key: links and unlinks two records
then: Expects the link's row added, then removed.

title: lathe remove removes a record with its parts and its own links
key: removes a record with its parts and its own links
then: Expects the record, its parts and its links gone.

title: lathe show shows a record with its parts, children and links
key: shows a record with its parts, children and links
then: Expects the record's columns, parts, children and links both ways.

title: A spec is written end to end with the lathe command
key: with the lathe command
then: Expects the written data to load with every key and check, and lathe check to pass.

title: A spec is written end to end with the MCP tools, as the plugin starts them
key: with the MCP tools, as the plugin starts them
then: Expects the same data as with the lathe command.

title: The MCP tools are add, set, move, link, unlink, remove, show, list, next_id and check
key: are add, set, move, link, unlink, remove, show, list, next_id and check
then: Expects exactly those tools.

title: A test whose file lacks its ID is reported as an error
when: Loads tests whose files lack their IDs, are gone, or name them.
then: Expects a `test-file-missing-id` error, a `test-file-missing` error, and nothing for the test whose file names it.

title: The MCP tools take input schemas generated from the schema description, product kinds included
key: take input schemas generated from the schema description, product kinds included

title: The add tool returns the row added, and a refusal with its reason
key: add returns the row added, and a refusal with its reason

title: The MCP server answers initialize, tools/list and tools/call over stdio
key: answers initialize, tools/list and tools/call over stdio
then: Expects each answered over stdio, and the tool list announced again when the tools change.

title: No skill tells the Agent to write spec files by hand
key: no skill tells the Agent to write spec files by hand
then: Expects no skill to tell the Agent to edit data files, only to use the tools.

title: Every example in the skills names real tables, columns and relations, with values of the columns' types
key: every example in the skills names real tables, columns and relations
then: Expects every example's table, columns and relation in the schema, with values of their types.

title: The MCP launcher starts the repo's own lathe mcp for the project folder
key: starts the repo's own lathe mcp for the project folder
then: Expects the repo's own lathe mcp to answer, and a reason when the folder is no Lathe repo.

title: A product's own kind takes effect on the next load, with its own table
when: Declares a product kind and adds a record of it in one write, then asks to remove the kind while the record is left.
then: Expects the next load to have the kind and its record, placed under its domain, with no error, and the removal of the kind refused.

title: A product kind or relation that names an undefined kind, repeats itself or has a bad field name is refused
when: Loads a product kind under a kind that does not exist, a kind declared twice, a relation from a kind that does not exist, and a field with a bad name.
then: Expects each refused, naming what it lacks, and no error for Lathe's schema or a product's own kinds.

title: The server has no way to change the meta-model
when: Sends POST and PUT requests to `/api/spec` and to schema-like paths, and a write to a meta table, on the running server.
then: Expects them refused, and the migrations unchanged.

title: A domain rule may sit under its domain alone, and a product cannot widen Lathe's own kinds
when: Loads a product with a rule under its domain and its own kinds, then declares a kind named domain_rule.
then: Expects the rule placed in its domain with no error, Lathe's domain_rule kind unchanged, and the declaration refused, naming domain_rule.

title: A product's own kind is added after Lathe's, with its own label, stage and obligation, and Lathe's kinds keep theirs
then: Expects the product's kind with its own label, stage, parent and obligation, after Lathe's kinds, which are the same as in a product with no kinds of its own.

title: A product relation with Lathe's name adds a pair and changes none of Lathe's
then: Expects one more pair, from a test to the product's kind, and Lathe's own proves pairs as they were.

title: A kind declared twice is refused, naming the file and line
when: Loads the same product kind twice.
then: Expects a primary-key refusal on line 2 of the declaration file, naming the kind and line 1.

title: Capabilities, patterns and the follows relation are in the schema
when: Loads a product.
then: Expects the `capability` kind under a domain with a required position, the `pattern` kind under a product with no required columns, use cases, flows and tests under a capability or a domain, and `follows` from a domain or a use case to a pattern, with no role.

title: Use cases, flows and tests may sit under a capability, and use cases follow patterns
when: Loads a fixture whose use case, flow and test sit under capabilities and whose use cases follow a pattern.
then: Expects no errors and no problem from the capability or pattern checks.

title: A record under a capability belongs to the capability's domain and counts in its coverage
then: Expects the capability and the records under it to carry the capability's domain, the pattern to carry no domain, and the requirements under capability use cases to be counted in the domain's coverage.

title: A position that is not a whole number is refused by the store
when: Loads capabilities with positions `first` and 2.5.
then: Expects each refused, naming the file and line, as not a whole number.

title: Two capabilities in one domain with the same position are refused; other domains may reuse it
when: Loads two capabilities with position 1 in one domain, and one with position 1 in another domain.
then: Expects the second refused as not unique, naming the first, and the other domain's capability loaded with no problem.

title: A use case directly under a domain that has capabilities is a warning
then: Expects one `use-case-outside-capability` warning for the use case under a domain with capabilities, and none for the use case under a domain without any.

title: A pattern's setting that is not a valid field name is refused by the store
when: Loads pattern settings named `Bad-Name` and `has space`, and a use case that follows a pattern with a setting named `title` but does not answer it.
then: Expects each bad name refused, and the `title` setting owed by the use case like any other.

title: A rule whose setting is not one of its pattern's settings is refused by the store
when: Loads a pattern rule naming a misspelled setting.
then: Expects a foreign-key refusal naming the file, the line and the setting.

title: An ID a record names in its text is kept as written, and makes no link
when: Loads records whose text names other records, one of them twice.
then: Expects the text kept as written, no links, and no list of named IDs on a record.

title: A token that is not an ID of this workspace is plain text and no problem
then: Expects text naming IDs that no record has, with unknown prefixes, to be kept and reported by nothing.

title: Text keeps every repeat as written, its own ID included
then: Expects a record's text to keep an ID named twice, and its own ID.

title: An ID in text that no record has is no warning: no check reads text for IDs
then: Expects no problem for a missing rule named in text, and `data-refused` as the engine's only problem of its own.

title: Only link tables link records: a link to a record that does not exist is refused, while text naming it is not
when: Loads a use case whose goal names a missing rule, then adds an applies link to it.
then: Expects the text accepted and the link refused as a foreign key.

title: A product relation adds a link table of its own, and Lathe's relations keep their roles, labels and descriptions
when: Loads a product with a relation of its own.
then: Expects the relation with its labels and description and its link, Lathe's own relations as in a product without one, and a flow's fulfills still counting as no design.

title: A flow step sits under a flow, needs a position, fulfills obligations and uses views, endpoints and components
when: Loads a flow written as steps.
then: Expects the `flow_step` kind under a flow with a required path and position, its seven relation pairs, and a step loaded with its position, path and links.

title: A step position that is not a whole number is refused by the store
when: Loads steps with positions `two` and 1.5.
then: Expects each refused, naming the file and line, as not a whole number.

title: Two steps on one path of a flow with the same position are refused; steps of other flows may share it
when: Loads two steps with one position on the main path of a flow, then on two paths, and steps of three flows with position 1.
then: Expects the second step on one path refused as not unique, and the others loaded with no step-order problem.

title: A step with no position is refused, and a path whose positions skip a number is reported once
when: Loads a step with no position, and a flow whose steps have positions 1, 2, 4 and 5.
then: Expects the first refused as missing a required column, and one `step-order` error on the first step after the gap, naming the missing number.

title: A step that fulfills something its flow does not carry out is a warning naming what it compared
then: Expects `flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow` for another use case's requirement, a rule only that use case applies, and an interaction requirement that fulfills it, each naming the flow's use cases.

title: A step may fulfill its flow's use case requirements, the rules they apply, and interaction requirements reached from them or under the flow
then: Expects no warning for steps that fulfill a requirement of the carried-out use case, a rule it applies, an endpoint interaction requirement that fulfills one of them, and an interaction requirement under the flow.

title: A flow with steps that fulfills something none of its steps does is a warning
then: Expects `flow-fulfills-differs-from-steps` on a flow that fulfills a rule none of its steps fulfills, naming the rule.

title: A flow may repeat or leave out its steps' fulfills, and a flow without steps is not compared
then: Expects no warning for a flow repeating one of its steps' links, one naming none, and one without steps.

title: A flow written as well-formed steps breaks nothing and raises no step problem
then: Expects no errors and no flow step problem in a well-formed workspace, and every flow step check to fire in the broken one.

title: A token that is the ID of a record is plain text, whatever its prefix: it is no link
then: Expects a use case's text naming another record kept as written, and no links.

title: A token starting with a product's or domain's ID and '-' is plain text, and no problem when no record has it
then: Expects text naming missing IDs with the domain's prefix kept, and no problem about them.

title: A token with any other prefix, such as STD- or SYS-, is plain text too
then: Expects text naming STD- and SYS- IDs kept, and no problem about them.

title: A bare product or domain ID in plain text is kept as written
then: Expects a domain's description naming the product and the domain, in plain text and in a code span, kept exactly.

title: A bare product or domain ID in a code span is kept as written, code span and all
then: Expects the product's description to keep its code span.

title: No ID in text, known or not, is a warning: Lathe has no check that reads text for IDs
then: Expects no `unknown-id-in-prose` problem, and no problem naming an ID written in another record's text.

title: lathe.config.json takes no idPrefixes: it is an unknown setting
when: Writes a config with `idPrefixes`.
then: Expects `loadConfig` and `loadWorkspace` to refuse it as an unknown setting, saying the settings are data.

title: Code spans and fences in text are stored exactly as written, spacing included
then: Expects a use case's notes, with a fence and code spans, kept exactly.

title: A kind's obligation is full, proof (proof only) or none (not an obligation)
then: Expects `pattern_rule` a proof-only obligation, `requirement` a full one and `pattern` none, and a product's own kinds declared proof and none read as such, with no errors.

title: The engine loads each kind's section and the folders in stage then order
then: Expects the default folders in order (Shared; Domain model, Use cases; Interaction design, Technical specification, Test plan) and every default kind's folder, with no folder problems.

title: A product's own kind is placed in one of the schema's folders, and Lathe's kinds keep theirs
when: Loads a product kind in the domain model folder.
then: Expects it in that folder, Lathe's kinds where they were, the folders unchanged, and no stage mismatch.

title: A kind naming a folder that is not listed is refused
when: Loads a product kind whose section is a folder the schema lacks, and one with no section.
then: Expects the first refused, naming the folder, and the second accepted.

title: A kind in another stage's folder is a section-stage-mismatch error; a product-level folder takes any stage
when: Loads a product kind of one stage in another stage's folder, one of no stage in a Design folder, and one in Shared.
then: Expects a `section-stage-mismatch` error for the first two, naming the kind's stage and the folder's, and none for Shared or Lathe's own kinds.

title: Every folder is a row of the schema, and a kind with no folder sits in none
when: Loads a product kind with no section.
then: Expects it in no folder, every kind's folder among the schema's folders, and no stage mismatch.

title: A layer sits in a domain or a layer with a position, and holds components, sub-layers and technical flows
then: Expects the `layer` kind under a layer or a domain with a required position in the Technical specification folder, components and technical flows under a layer or a domain and nothing else under a layer, and a product's own layers as records, with no errors.

title: A layer position that is not a whole number is refused by the store
when: Loads layers with positions `first` and 2.5.
then: Expects each refused as not a whole number.

title: Two layers in one domain with the same position are errors; another domain may reuse it
then: Expects `layer-order` errors on two layers of one domain with the same position, each naming the other, and none for a layer of another domain with that position.

title: A component directly in a domain that has layers is a warning; a domain without layers is fine
then: Expects one `component-outside-layer` warning for the component under a domain with layers, and none for a component in a layer or in a domain with no layers.

title: A component in a layer belongs to the layer's domain and product
then: Expects a layer and the components under it to have the layer's domain and product, with the layer as the components' parent.

title: Coverage counts a component in a layer exactly as one directly in the domain
when: Loads two domains alike except that one puts its components in layers.
then: Expects the same coverage for both, IDs aside: the same designed and built requirements and domain rules, and the same owed pattern rule designed by the layered component.

title: Every check reports a domain with layers exactly as the same domain without them
when: Loads the same two domains.
then: Expects the same problems for both, IDs aside, including the component file, unproved, proof-still-owed and proof-counts-nowhere warnings, and no flow step warnings.

title: An entity sits under an aggregate in the domain model, needs a role, and links to entities by has_one, has_many and refers_to
then: Expects the `entity` kind's stage, folder, parent and required role, its three relations to entities, and an entity's links.

title: An entity's fields are its entity_field rows, in position order; other kinds have none
then: Expects an entity's fields with their names, meanings, types and examples, in order, an example optional, and no entity_field rows on other kinds.

title: A field needs a name, a meaning and a type, and a name once per entity: the store refuses the rest
when: Loads fields without a name, a meaning or a type, with a blank name, and a name twice in one entity.
then: Expects each refused, naming the file, and the repeat as not unique.

title: A role other than root or child, or none, is refused by the store
when: Loads entities with roles `leaf` and `ROOT`, and one with no role.
then: Expects each refused: a role that is not one of root and child, and a missing required column.

title: An aggregate with entities and no root, or more than one, is refused by the store
when: Loads an aggregate with two roots and one with none.
then: Expects each refused by the aggregate-root validation, naming how many roots it has, and an aggregate with no entities accepted.

title: An entity that lists no fields is an entity-fields error
then: Expects one `entity-fields` error, on the entity with no fields, saying to add them.

title: has_one or has_many to an entity in another aggregate is a has-crosses-aggregate error; refers_to may cross aggregates and domains
then: Expects a `has-crosses-aggregate` error for a has_many into another aggregate, and none for refers_to across aggregates and domains.

title: A child entity its root does not reach by has_one or has_many is an entity-unreferenced warning
then: Expects warnings for children nothing reaches, reached only from an unreached child, or only referring to the root, and none for a child reached through another child.

title: A well-formed domain model with entities gives no problems, and each entity check fails on its own fixture
then: Expects no problems from the good fixture, and every entity check among the broken fixture's problems.

title: The reference holds every kind, table, relation, folder and check of Lathe's schema
when: Builds Lathe's reference.
then: Expects a use case's facts, parents, children and ID convention, the obligation values, each kind's table with its columns, keys and references, a part table, relation pairs and roles, the folders in order, every check row in run order and the engine's own `data-refused`.

title: A product's reference shows its own kinds and relations and its own checks
then: Expects a product's own kind with its table and relation pair, and its own checks after Lathe's.

title: The committed REFERENCE.md is the reference as the reference script writes it
when: Renders Lathe's reference.
then: Expects it to equal the committed `lathe/REFERENCE.md`.

title: The Markdown gives the data model, then kinds with their tables, other tables, relations, folders and checks, each with an anchor
then: Expects the sections in order, an anchor for each kind, table, relation, folder and check, and every link inside the document to land on an anchor.

title: A product kind or relation without a description, or a check without its explanation, is refused
when: Loads a product kind with a blank description, a relation with none, and a check row with no explanation.
then: Expects each refused.

title: A product's own checks are held to the same rule, and Lathe's are all documented
then: Expects every kind, table and check of Lathe's described, and a product's own checks with their summary and explanation.

title: The reference script prints a product's reference, or writes it with --out
when: Runs the reference script for a product with its own kinds, with `--print` and with `--out`.
then: Expects the rendered reference in both.

title: GET /api/reference serves the product reference as JSON
when: Calls the API for a product with its own kinds.
then: Expects 200 with its reference as JSON.

title: A product relation without both labels is refused
when: Loads product relations without a reverse label and with a blank forward label.
then: Expects each refused, and every one of Lathe's relations labeled both ways.

title: The reference reads each relation by its labels
when: Builds the default reference.
then: Expects each relation rule to carry its forward and reverse labels, the relations table to show both, and a requirement's links in to read as "Designed by" and "Proved by".

title: A domain event sits under an aggregate in the domain model, is raised_by an entity, and is reacted to by aggregates, use cases and components
then: Expects the `domain_event` kind's stage, folder and parent, the `raised_by` and three `reacts_to` pairs with their labels, a reacts_to link from an aggregate, and one from a domain rule refused.

title: A domain event's fields are its event_field rows, in position order, as an entity's are
then: Expects an event's fields in order, none for an event with no fields, and no event_field rows on other kinds.

title: A domain event with no fields is an entity-fields error naming it as an event; a field without a name, or named twice, is refused
then: Expects an `entity-fields` error naming the event, and a blank or repeated field name refused.

title: A raised_by that names an entity of another aggregate is a raised-by-outside-aggregate error; a missing raised_by is not
then: Expects one `raised-by-outside-aggregate` error naming both aggregates, none for an event with no raised_by, and a raised_by to a missing record or to an aggregate refused.

title: An event that nothing reacts to is an event-unheard warning that says this can be fine; a reacts_to from any record hears it
then: Expects `event-unheard` warnings for exactly the events no reacts_to link targets, with the message that says this can be fine.

title: A title with no past form as its last word or after its first is an event-tense warning
then: Expects `event-tense` warnings for Open loan and Repair need, and none for titles ending in -ed, with an irregular past form, with a past form after the subject, of one word, or in capitals with a hyphen.

title: Steps are numbered within their path, main by default, and path names match trimmed in any case
then: Expects no problem on a flow whose main path is written main and whose refused path, written as refused and as " Refused ", is numbered 1, 2 on its own.

title: A repeated position on a path is refused by the store, and a path whose numbering skips is a step-order error
then: Expects one `step-order` error per path whose positions skip, on the first step after the first gap and naming every missing number, and a second step with the same flow, path and position refused.

title: A position that is not a whole number, or a step with none, is refused, so a gap is only ever between whole numbers
then: Expects a step with no position and one with position `x` refused, and nothing reported for a flow numbered 1, 2, 3 on two paths.

title: A domain rule may sit under an entity, and a layer under a layer
then: Expects `domain_rule` to name aggregate, domain and entity as parent kinds, `layer` to name domain and layer, and no `parent-kind-not-allowed` problem in the twin fixture.

title: A rule under an entity, and a component in a sub-layer, belong to their ancestors' domain and product
then: Expects a domain rule under an entity, a sub-layer and a component in it to carry the domain and product of their ancestors.

title: An entity's fields are entity_field rows, each with a name, a meaning and a type
then: Expects twin entities' fields equal, with no `entity-fields` problem, and a field without its meaning refused.

title: A malformed data file is a data-refused error naming the file and line, not a crash
when: Loads a product whose `data/aggregate.jsonl` holds a line that is not JSON.
then: Expects one `data-refused` error with no record, naming `data/aggregate.jsonl:2`, no records loaded and no other problem.

title: The check prints errors, then warnings, then coverage with designed, built and proved
when: Runs `lathe check` on the broken-tests and unfinished fixtures.
then: Expects the errors section, then the warnings, then the coverage lines and each domain's tests line, each coverage line giving designed, built, proved and planned counts and the gaps.

title: The check exits 1 on any error and 0 otherwise, whatever the warnings
when: Runs `lathe check` on fixtures with errors, with no problems and with only warnings, and on a data file whose row has a column its table does not have.
then: Expects status 1, 0, 0 and 1, the last reporting `data-refused` with `data/product.jsonl:1`.

title: With --json the check prints the whole workspace
when: Runs `lathe check --json`.
then: Expects its output to parse to the same `Workspace` that `loadWorkspace` returns.

title: A new check needs only a new check row
when: Adds one check row to a copy of the good fixture through the store, with no change to the engine.
then: Expects the row's problem as the workspace's only problem, named after the check.

title: Checks can read every typed table, with file facts already computed
when: Runs a check that counts the record registry, the links, the test table and the meta-model tables, and reads the file facts.
then: Expects the counts to match the workspace, and each file fact (the file exists, the test's file names its ID) to match the fixture.

title: Every check runs, in position order, even after one fails
when: Runs three check rows, the second of which reads a table that does not exist.
then: Expects their problems in position order, with the failing check reported as one error saying it could not run.

title: Each check is one SELECT query in its row, and Lathe's checks are named and placed in order
when: Reads every row of Lathe's `lathe/data/check.jsonl`.
then: Expects positions 1, 2, 3 and so on with no product, and each query a single SELECT or WITH statement.

title: Data the schema refuses is an error, and work to do is a warning
when: Loads every fixture, one with a use case that has no requirements, and one whose use case applies a rule that does not exist.
then: Expects every problem of a work-to-do check to be a warning and every other to be an error, every kind of work to do to appear, and the link to the missing rule to be one `data-refused` error.

title: Every problem names its check and, when it has one, its record
then: Expects every problem in every fixture to name its check in lower case with hyphens, to end as a sentence, and to name its record, whose ID its message contains.

title: IDs in code spans and fenced code blocks are kept with the text as written
when: Loads text with IDs in single and double backtick spans and in backtick and tilde fences.
then: Expects each ID kept in the text as written, and no problem about any of them.

title: A domain rule that no use case applies is a warning
when: Loads a domain with one rule a use case applies and one nothing applies.
then: Expects `rule-not-applied` on the second only.

title: A use case that no flow carries out is a warning, once its domain has flows
when: Loads a domain with a flow that carries out one use case and a flow that only fulfills another's requirement, and a second domain with no flows.
then: Expects `use-case-without-flow` on the second use case only.

title: An interaction requirement that fulfills nothing is a warning
when: Loads a view with two interaction requirements, one with a `fulfills` link.
then: Expects the warning on the other.

title: A domain_rule test proving only requirements, or an acceptance test proving only domain rules, is a warning
then: Expects `test-type-mismatch` on each of the three mismatched tests, one with its type in another letter case, naming what each proves.

title: A unit test, another test type, or a test proving both kinds is not compared
then: Expects no `test-type-mismatch` on a unit test proving a requirement, an acceptance test proving both kinds, a matching rule test, an integration test, or a rule test proving an interaction requirement.

title: Structural gaps are warnings and break nothing
then: Expects every structural check to fire in the warnings fixture, each as a warning, with no errors, and none in a workspace without the gaps.

title: A relation pair declared twice is refused, naming the file and line
when: Declares one product relation twice.
then: Expects one `primary-key` refusal naming `data/product_relation.jsonl`, line 3.

title: A test given its rule's ID is one unique-id refusal, and no link to the rule is refused with it
when: Adds a test whose ID is a domain rule's ID.
then: Expects one `unique-id` refusal on the test, naming `data/test.jsonl` line 2 and the rule's file and line, and no refusal of the links to the rule.

title: A link or parent that the schema does not allow is refused once, naming what it may be
when: Adds an `implements` link to a domain rule, and a question with a column for a domain rule as its parent.
then: Expects one foreign-key refusal naming the kinds the link's end accepts (endpoint, view), and one `column` refusal for the column a question does not have.

title: An unknown parent is refused once, as a foreign key naming the missing record
when: Adds a use case under a capability that does not exist.
then: Expects one foreign-key refusal: `capability_id "TL-LEND-CAP09" names no capability`.

title: A product check runs after Lathe's checks, against the same tables
when: Loads a product whose own check row reads the typed tables.
then: Expects its warnings after every problem from Lathe's checks, each with the severity its row gives.

title: A product check's name comes from its row, not from a check column its query returns
when: Loads a product check whose query returns `house-rule` in a check column.
then: Expects its problems under the row's name, `one-record-view-per-aggregate`, and none under `house-rule`.

title: A one Record view use case per aggregate house rule is carried as a product check
when: Encodes a product's house rule as a product check against three aggregates with one, none and two Record view use cases.
then: Expects warnings on the second and third only, naming the two use cases.

title: A product check named like one of Lathe's checks is refused by the store, so it never runs
when: Adds a product check named `unproved` through the store, then writes the same row into the product's `data/check.jsonl`.
then: Expects a `primary-key` refusal naming Lathe's `lathe/data/check.jsonl`, then a `data-refused` error when the data loads, and the check never run.

title: A product check that fails to run is an error naming the check
when: Loads a product whose check `broken` reads a table that does not exist.
then: Expects one error with no record under `broken`, saying the check could not run.

title: A product names no checks folder: lathe.config.json refuses a checks setting, since checks are rows
when: Loads a product whose `lathe.config.json` names a `checks` folder.
then: Expects the load to stop with `unknown setting "checks"`.

title: Without check rows of its own only Lathe's checks run
when: Loads the good fixture, which has no check rows of its own.
then: Expects no errors, and every problem from one of Lathe's checks.

title: A step whose flow carries out nothing is not compared, and a link to a missing target is refused by the store
when: Loads a flow that carries out no use case, and adds a step's `fulfills` link to a record that does not exist.
then: Expects no step warning for that flow, and the link refused as a foreign key naming no obligation.

title: Owed and silent proofs are warnings, never errors, and a workspace without them has none
then: Expects all three checks to report only warnings in a workspace with no errors, and none in the `good` fixture.

title: A record with more children of one kind than maxChildren is a warning naming the parent, kind and count
when: With `max_children` 3.
then: Expects a `too-many-children` warning for an aggregate with 4 domain rules, naming it, the kind and the count, and saying to add a level between them.

title: A record with exactly maxChildren children of a kind is not reported
when: With `max_children` 3.
then: Expects no warning for an aggregate with 3 domain rules.

title: Children are counted per kind
then: Expects a domain with 4 capabilities, 2 aggregates and 2 layers to be reported once, for its capabilities only.

title: Tests are never counted, however many a record holds
then: Expects no warning for a domain holding 5 tests directly, with `max_children` 3.

title: Without the setting, maxChildren is 15
when: With no `product_setting` row.
then: Expects `DEFAULT_MAX_CHILDREN` to be 15, a warning for a domain with 16 components, and none for one with 15.

title: maxChildren is read from the product's product_setting row, max_children
when: Loads a product whose `product_setting` row gives `max_children` 3.
then: Expects `too-many-children` on the three records over 3, each message naming the product's max_children setting.

title: A maxChildren that is not a whole number of at least 1 is refused
when: Gives `max_children` the values 0, a word and 2.5.
then: Expects the store to refuse 0 by the table's check, and the word and 2.5 as values of the wrong type.

title: A capability with exactly one child is a warning naming the child
then: Expects a `lone-child` warning for a capability holding one use case, naming both and saying to merge it into a neighboring capability or give it more.

title: A layer with exactly one child is a warning
then: Expects a `lone-child` warning for a layer holding one component.

title: A lone child counts every kind of child, and only the record's own children
then: Expects no warning for a capability holding a use case and a flow, and a warning for one holding one use case that has two requirements.

title: A capability or layer with no children, or with two, is not reported
then: Expects `lone-child` warnings only for the capability and the layer with one child, and none for an empty capability or ones with two children.

title: Too many children and a lone child are warnings, never errors
then: Expects every `too-many-children` and `lone-child` problem to be a warning, and no errors in either fixture.

title: A check reads the maxChildren setting from the product_setting table
when: Loads a product whose own check reads its `product_setting` row.
then: Expects the check to see `max_children` 3.

title: Every check row has a one-sentence summary, an explanation and a severity that matches its query
when: Reads every row of Lathe's `lathe/data/check.jsonl`.
then: Expects a one-sentence summary, an explanation, and the severity `error_or_warning` exactly when its query returns a severity column.

title: A check row is read as summary, explanation, severity and kinds, and one without them is refused
when: Builds the reference, and loads a check row without an explanation and one with an unknown severity.
then: Expects the reference to hold a row's summary, explanation, severity and kinds, and the store to refuse the other two.

title: A flow's steps are counted per path, and the message names a path other than main
when: Loads a flow with three steps on main and three on refused under a limit of 3.
then: Expects no warning; then a flow with four steps on refused, and expects one warning naming that path.

title: A space's Checks page lists its product's problems, errors first, grouped by check
then: Checks the space's error and warning totals, its groups by check with errors before warnings, each problem's link to its record, then the workspace's problem under Workspace, and none of the other product's.

title: A component that satisfies nothing is a warning
when: Loads components that satisfy a requirement, only implement a view and depend on another component, or link nothing they design.
then: Expects the warning on the last two only.

title: A test that proves and supports nothing is a warning
when: Loads tests that prove a requirement, only support a domain rule, are only planned, only run a flow and cover a component, or have no links.
then: Expects the warning on the last two only.

title: A component or test with no purpose is a warning that breaks nothing
then: Expects both checks to report only warnings with no errors, a `satisfies` link to a record that is gone to be refused by the store, and no warning where every component and test serves an obligation.

title: A link from a record of one product to a record of another is refused, whatever the relation; an ID in text is not a link
when: Adds an `involves` and an `applies` link from one product's records to another's, and loads text naming another product's ID.
then: Expects each link refused by `link-crosses-product`, and the text kept as written, with no link and no problem.

title: too-many-children counts grouped requirements per group, groups compared in any case
when: Loads a use case with one ungrouped requirement, five in Validation (one written in lower case with a trailing space) and three in Paging under a limit of 3.
then: Expects one warning, naming Validation; a pattern whose rules fall into groups of two, one and two gets none.

title: A group with one member is a lone-child warning on its parent, standard rules included
then: Expects a view whose Errors group holds one interaction requirement, a pattern whose Paging group holds one rule, and a standard whose Logging group holds one rule, each to get a `lone-child` warning naming the group and its member.

title: The guard hook refuses an edit of a data file and points at the tools
key: refuses an edit of a data file and points at the tools
when: Runs the guard hook on an Edit of `data/product.jsonl`, and on a Write of a relative path in a data folder that `lathe.config.json` names.
then: Expects the permission decision deny, with a reason saying the file is Lathe data to change only with Lathe's MCP tools.

title: The guard hook lets every other edit through, silently
key: lets every other edit through, silently
when: Runs the guard hook on a source file, a `.jsonl` file outside the data folder, a data folder outside any Lathe repo, and empty input.
then: Expects exit status 0 and no output each time.

title: The plugin declares the MCP server and the guard hook, and every script they name exists
key: declares the MCP server and the guard hook, and every script they name exists
when: Reads the plugin's `.mcp.json` and `hooks/hooks.json`.
then: Expects the lathe MCP server and one PreToolUse hook, naming `scripts/mcp-server.mjs` and `scripts/guard-data-files.mjs`, both of which exist.

title: Every page has its own address, and back and forward move between pages
when: Parses every spec address into its page, and an old one as missing, opens a record page directly from its address, follows menu links.
then: Checks that the browser's back and forward buttons return to the earlier pages.

title: The menu lists each product and its domains beside the Tools section
when: Renders the app with two products.
then: Checks the Tools section and no Diagrams section, each product in the rail, and the current space's domains as links in the panel.

title: The domain page groups records by stage and folder, with rules and requirements nested
then: Checks the Define stage's folders (Domain model, with aggregates and their rules nested; Use cases, with requirements nested) and the Design stage's folders (Interaction design, holding flows, views and endpoints under their own headings; Technical specification; Test plan), in that order, with their key fields.

title: The search box filters records by ID or title as you type
when: Types a title fragment and an ID fragment into the search box.
then: Checks which records stay shown, then clears it and checks that every record is back.

title: The domain page lists its coverage gaps and its problems
then: Checks the coverage gaps, each with the link that is missing, the "not proved" tag on the record's row, and the domain's problems, errors first and no other domain's.

title: The record page shows the ID, kind, title, text fields as Markdown, parent and children
when: Opens a use case.
then: Checks its ID, kind, actor, data file, its goal rendered as Markdown, parent link and child requirements; then checks that Markdown in a text field is rendered.

title: The record page shows links out and in, grouped and named by their labels, each clickable
when: Opens a requirement.
then: Checks its incoming links grouped under their reverse labels (Carried out in, Designed by, Proved by), follows the satisfying component's link, and checks that component's outgoing links under their forward labels (Implements, Satisfies).

title: A record's text is sanitized before it is shown
when: Renders a text field holding a script, an image with an onerror handler and a javascript: link, and Markdown holding an iframe and an onclick.
then: Checks that none of them reaches the page or runs.

title: The record page lists every problem about the record
then: Checks that a test with a missing file shows its error and badge, and that a record with no problems says so.

title: Every record ID a page shows is a real link to that record
when: Opens every product, domain, record.
then: Checks page of the fixture and checks that each record ID shown sits in an `<a href>` to that record's page.

title: In the graph a domain reaches its components through Design, Technical specification, then a layer, one level each
then: Expects a "Layers (3)" folder at depth 1 with only parent lines, the layers one column right of it, and from a layer its folder to the left and its components to the right, in the model and on the canvas.

title: A group page of tests reads them in the test plan's groups
then: Expects a domain's Tests group page to head its members by the five test groups, holding the domain's own tests.

title: Group labels name kinds through plural(), and opened groups last the session
when: Renames two kinds.
then: Expects "Parts outside any layer" and "Stories outside any capability"; then expects an opened layer row remembered in session storage only.

title: In the graph a capability with 7 use cases shows them directly, with no folder
then: Expects a capability with seven use cases and nothing else to have no group node and a parent line to each use case, and a layer to point straight at its components.

title: A split by kind or test group appears only with several to tell apart
then: Expects a test plan with one group to list its tests directly in the nav and on the domain page; one with acceptance tests only to drop that level but keep its use cases; a folder of one kind to have no per-kind heading while one of three kinds has three; and children of one kind to carry no kind tag while a product's mixed children do.

title: In the graph a domain's Test plan folder holds the test plan's groups, from the same folder model
then: Expects the Tests folder's group nodes with their counts and the folder model's keys, a test reached through its folder, acceptance, capability and use case one column each left to right, tests hanging straight under the folder when one group has them all, and a test group's own page.

title: The graph trail names a record by title and ID, a group by name alone
then: Expects the current item to read as a long title with its ID in parentheses in code style, its full text in its tooltip, and a test group's page to show "Acceptance tests" with its parent in the tooltip.

title: The glide follows the shared easing: CSS's ease, read from the motion tokens
then: Checks the easing curve against CSS's ease walked finely, a pan halfway through the time most of the way there, and the motion tokens parsed as the stylesheet writes them.

title: A plain open replaces the one preview tab in place, a page open in a tab activates it, and keeping makes a tab lasting
when: Opens pages in an empty tab set.
then: Expects each plain open to replace the preview tab where it sits, keeping its key, with its state made from the tab that was active; a kept tab to stay when the next page opens beside it; a page already open to activate its tab; a kept open to add a lasting tab after the active one; and never two previews or two tabs for one page.

title: Closing the active tab activates its right neighbor, or else the left; closing the last leaves it as a preview; cycling wraps
when: Cycles three lasting tabs both ways past each end, closes the active first tab.
then: Expects its right neighbor active, closes an inactive tab and expects the active one kept, closes the rightmost and expects its left neighbor, and closes the last and expects it still open, as the preview. Unknown keys change nothing.

title: Each tab keeps its own state, and a stored set is read back with anything malformed dropped
when: Changes one tab's state.
then: Expects the other's unchanged; reads back a stored set with a bad path and a bad state and expects only the good tabs, the last of two stored previews kept as the preview, and an unknown active tab replaced by the first.

title: A plain open replaces the italic preview tab, a double-click keeps it, a page already open activates its tab, and Back reopens a closed page as the preview
when: Opens a record.
then: Expects one preview tab with its ID in mono, labeling the tab panel; follows a wiki link and expects the preview replaced; double-clicks it to keep it and expects the next page in a new preview beside it, a group's tab with its label and no ID; follows a link to the kept page and expects its tab active, no second tab; clicks a tab and expects the address to follow; closes it, goes Back and expects it reopened as the preview.

title: Closing by button, middle-click or Alt+Shift+W activates the right neighbor or else the left, and the last tab stays as the preview
when: Keeps three tabs, activates the middle one and closes it with Alt+Shift+W, expecting the right neighbor and its address; middle-clicks the rightmost.
then: Expects the left neighbor; closes the last and expects it still open, as the preview.

title: Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle, the keep command keeps the preview, and on the focused strip the arrow keys move and Delete closes
then: Expects the four tab commands in the keymap; keeps the preview with Alt+K then Enter (off a Mac); cycles with Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab; expects only the active tab in the Tab order, the arrow key to move focus, Enter to activate and Delete to close the focused tab, with focus left on the tab now active. Expects the active tab's close button to carry the close command's keys.

title: Each tab keeps its own views, wiki scroll and graph settings, and switching its views keeps it open
when: Opens the graph on a preview tab.
then: Expects it kept, sets the depth and scrolls the wiki; opens another page and expects it to start with the same views and depth at the top, then changes them; returns to the first tab and expects its two panes, depth and scroll back, and to the second for its wiki alone. A link naming other views to a page open in a tab shows the tab as it was and rewrites the address to its views.

title: Each space keeps its own tabs, and switching spaces swaps the tab set
when: Opens two tabs in one product's space, moves to another product's page.
then: Expects only its tab, then switches back by the rail and expects the first space's two tabs again.

title: Pages only read GET /api/spec until the person acts: the record actions are the only controls that lead to a write, and opening a page or searching it sends none
when: Opens every spec page, types in its search boxes, and looks for forms, inputs and buttons before any record action is chosen.
then: Expects no form, editor or input but the search boxes, every button a plain button, the only buttons that lead to a write inside the record's Change toolbar, and no request but GET /api/spec.

title: A list of children or members of one kind is titled by that kind
then: Expects an aggregate's page to title its children "Domain rules", with the list named "Domain rules of DM-SHOP-A1", and the side bar not to repeat them, nor a use case's requirements; a row's nested list to be named by its kind; a product's mixed children, in its side bar, to stay "Children", tagged by kind; a group's members on the wiki group page to be titled "Use cases", with the list named "Use cases of DM-SHOP/use_case"; and a renamed kind to title the list with its own label.

title: The Model view is offered only on domain, aggregate and entity pages, opens after Wiki and Graph, and an address naming it elsewhere drops it
then: Expects the views a domain, aggregate, entity, use case and product offer, a use case opened with `?view=graph,model` to show only its graph, and on an aggregate Ctrl+4 to open the Model pane third, with the View toggles, and Alt+M to close it.

title: A domain's ERD draws each aggregate with its root and entity count, one many-to-one line per aggregate pair and direction, relates_to dashed as a fallback, and another domain's aggregates gray
when: Builds a domain's ERD.
then: Expects its four aggregates and the referenced one from another domain, gray with its domain in parentheses, the root and entity count on a box, two references between one pair drawn as one line, and a dashed relates_to line for an aggregate whose entities refer to none; then draws it and expects the boxes and lines.

title: An aggregate's ERD shows each entity's title, root mark and fields with their kind of value, crow's-foot ends by cardinality, and entities from elsewhere labeled with their owner
when: Builds an aggregate's ERD.
then: Expects the root's fields with their kinds, an entity of another aggregate labeled with it, one of another domain gray and labeled with its domain and aggregate, one-one, one-many and many-one ends, and lines from box edge to box edge; then draws it and expects the root mark, the fields list and the ends.

title: An entity page draws its aggregate's ERD with the entity highlighted
when: Opens a child entity in the Model view.
then: Expects its aggregate's ERD with only that entity highlighted, and the key naming it.

title: An ERD draws exactly one line per relationship link
when: Builds every aggregate's ERD in a domain.
then: Expects their lines together to be exactly the domain's entity relationship links, each once, and the domain's ERD to draw one line per aggregate pair and direction, standing for every refers_to link that crosses aggregates.

title: Above a graph or a model pane the page title keeps one fixed height; in the wiki pane it wraps
when: Opens an aggregate in the Graph view and an entity in the Model view.
then: Expects the title area to have the fixed-height class, with the whole title as its tooltip and a set height, one line each, in the stylesheet; with the wiki open on the left it does not.

title: The camera frames the focus and the levels the depth shows below it, the parent at the left edge
when: Frames a domain at depths 1 and 2, a stage at depth 3, a use case and a short group in a wide level, on a canvas of 1000 by 800.
then: Expects the focus within the padding top to bottom and centered on its middle, the framed levels fitting the canvas, the parent in view in a strip at the left edge with the focus right of it, deeper frames never zooming in further, every frame within the camera's zoom limit and a leaf framed short of it, and the whole map fitting the overview.

title: Depth counts levels of the tree below the focus, stages and folders included, with the parent kept
when: Frames a requirement at depths 1 to 3 (the same picture: it has nothing below it), the Define stage at each depth (its folders, their records, their children), and an aggregate.
then: Expects the parent kept, each node's distance and the node it was reached from, only parent lines, and no sibling or link.

title: Focusing a child glides the camera on the shared motion, and no box moves or changes size
when: Opens a use case's graph, framed at once, clicks its requirement.
then: Expects the camera to glide there over several frames and end framing it, every box drawn before and after at the same place and size, and Back gliding back.

title: Under reduced motion focusing frames the new focus at once
when: Asks for reduced motion, clicks a requirement in its use case's graph.
then: Expects one camera move, straight to the framed view.

title: A click on a row opens its record, and a click on its chevron or second link does what that control does
then: On a domain page, a click on a row's padding reaches its stretched row link and opens the record. jsdom has no layout, so the test sends the click where the browser does: to the topmost element at that point, which is the link's `::after`, that is the link itself; the stylesheet rules that make this so are proved by `LA-PLT-T52`. The link is a real `href`, so Cmd/Ctrl-click is left to the browser and opens a new tab. A click on a row's fold chevron opens the row and stays on the page; a click on a second link in the row, a pattern's "followed by" use case, opens that use case instead. Right and Left arrow keys still open and close a tree row.

title: By touch, a first tap on a graph node selects it and a second tap or the Open chip opens it
when: On a touch screen, taps a graph node on the canvas.
then: Expects the address unchanged, the node drawn as selected and its box in the keyboard layer outlined, and a card naming it; a tap on the canvas away from every box lets go; the Open chip opens it. `isTap` reads a mouse as a click and a finger or a pen as a tap.

title: A selected row is the whole row
when: Opens a domain page and a record page.
then: Expects one selected nav row each, the row holding the current link (and the domain's fold chevron), indented by its depth; and in the stylesheet the row spanning the panel with padding for its depth, the selection tint and steel text, no inset bar, no indent from the lists, the whole-row hover tint and the 1 px keyboard outline.

title: No page shows a relation code as a heading or label
when: Opens every record of a workspace with a record of each kind.
then: Expects no heading, field label, table header, legend, label or caption to read as a relation code ("satisfies", "proves", "depends on", "proves this"), and the graph's edge, legend and connection labels and the Model view's line titles to read the meta-model's labels.

title: A flow with several paths shows a table per path, the main path first
when: Gives a flow steps on the main path (no path), an api path and a refused path written in mixed case.
then: Expects three tables headed Main path, Api path and Refused path, each in its own step order.

title: Sub-layers nest in Technical specification, and a domain rule under an entity sits under it
when: Adds a sub-layer with a component inside a layer.
then: Expects the layer's group to hold the sub-layer's group and the component's branch to open through both layers; adds a domain rule under an entity, and expects the aggregate's page to list the entity with the rule folded under it and the rule's branch to open to the domain model.

title: A product's and a domain's one page, at its ID, shows its text, its facts, its links both ways and its problems
when: Opens a product and a domain at their IDs.
then: Expects its text in the wiki, the parent, data file, links out, links in and problems in the side bar, and no link to a second overview page.

title: The Links switch adds the records the focused record links to and from, one hop, in focus, with their links
when: Turns Links on at a requirement.
then: Expects what satisfies, fulfills and proves it, one step away and reached from it, with their links and no ring of their own; none with Links off; only the focus's own links at depth 3; and the same result on every call.

title: Depth counts levels below a domain and a use case, as a file explorer does
when: Frames a domain at depths 1 to 3.
then: Expects its stages, then their folders, then what is in them, one level more each time; and a use case in a capability, its capability the only node above it at every depth.

title: The graph's tree is the nav's tree
then: Expects a domain's stages and folders in the nav's order and counts, Capabilities as one list, a capability's use cases as its children with its test in the Test plan, Interaction design split by kind, Technical specification's layers then components, the product's Shared folder before its domains, and every child's parent to be the node that lists it.
