title: The Links switch is off by default, has a tooltip and the shortcut l, draws the center's links dashed, and is kept while walking
when: Opens a requirement's graph.
then: Expects the Links button unpressed with its shortcut, presses l, expects the linked records and three dashed link lines (and no tree line among them), then walks to the view and expects Links still on.

title: Filters have a Minimap switch, off by default and kept while walking, and the minimap is an overview of the whole map
when: Opens Filters.
then: Expects a Minimap switch, off, no context ring switch, and the trace preset worded with the relations' labels; switches the minimap on and expects an overview of the map's upper levels, the focus solid and the view outlined, still there after walking on.

title: Alt+Up, Alt+Down and Alt+Shift+Left and Right step through the tree, from the keyboard and from buttons
then: Expects the step targets of a use case, a folder and the product, the step buttons with their keys, and Alt+Down, Alt+Up, the step-out button and Alt+Shift+Left moving the center.

title: Filters hide kinds and relations and paths through them, never the focus
when: Hides tests, then the satisfies relation, then views.
then: Expects the hidden records and lines to go, nothing to be reached through them, and the focus to stay even when its own kind is hidden.

title: Hovering or focusing a box spotlights it, its lines and the boxes it joins, and leaving restores the picture
when: With Links on, focuses a linked view.
then: Expects it, the requirement and the line between them lit and the rest dimmed, and blurring it to restore the picture.

title: An aggregate's ERD shows what its referenced entities refer to one ring out; a domain's ERD fades other domains' aggregates
then: Expects the Loan ERD's own and referenced entities in focus, Member's Account as context with its line, nothing further, and the domain ERD's other-domain aggregate faded.

title: The ERD frames its boxes in focus only, and its context boxes are out of focus
then: Expects the framed boxes to leave out the ring, and on the page the ring box faded and aria-hidden, its line faded, and the key explaining it.

title: A stage or folder group page names the group by its own name, not by a kind
when: Opens a domain's Define stage page.
then: Expects its intro and the side bar to say "Define", never "Defines".

title: A tab keeps the graph's Links switch across a reload
when: Turns the graph's Links switch on, reloads the page.
then: Expects the same tab to come back with Links still on.

title: An aggregate's ERD draws each of its domain events as a spark flag with a short line from the entity raising it, and the aggregates reacting to it as faded context at the end of a dashed reacts-to line
when: Builds an aggregate's ERD with three events (one raised by time passing).
then: Expects a flag per event with its fields, a plain-ended line from each raising entity, a dashed line with an arrow to each reacting aggregate (faded; another domain's gray and named; the aggregate's reaction to its own event and a use case's drawing nothing), the layering that keeps the raised-by lines short, and an event's page scoping to its aggregate's ERD with its pill picked out. Renders the Model view and expects the pills, their accessible names, the lines' tooltips, a click on a pill going to the event, the event's own page in the Model view with its pill picked out, and the spark tokens in the stylesheet.

title: The ERD's key explains the event flag, the raised-by line and the dashed reacts-to line in the relations' own words, and keeps its one height
when: Opens an aggregate's and a domain's ERD.
then: Expects the key's Domain events list to explain the flag, "Raised by" and "Reacts to" (from the meta-model's labels) as each diagram draws them, an event's own key to say "This event", and the key's fixed height in the stylesheet.

title: Events sit under their aggregate through a "Domain events" group, are drawn as spark flags, and their reacts_to links are dashed, labeled from the meta-model and drawn with the Links switch
then: Expects the graph's tree to put an aggregate's events under its "Domain events" group, the Links switch to add an event's reacts_to and raised_by edges (and not without it), and their line style to be `event`. Renders the graph on an event, turns Links on, and expects the dashed spark edges labeled "Reacts to" and "Raised by", the event node as a spark pill and its group as a plain group.

title: GET /api/history lists the commits that changed a record's rows, newest first, with the columns each changed and the uncommitted changes
when: Against a temporary git repo of the good fixture with two commits that change the use case's row, one that changes another file, and a change not committed.
then: Expects the record's data file found from the data by its ID, the commits that changed its rows newest first with their author, date, subject and hash, the columns each commit changed with their values before and after, the changes not committed yet first, and nothing for a commit that changed only other rows.

title: GET /api/history answers 404 for an unknown record, 400 without an ID, and says calmly when the folder is not a git repo
then: Expects 404 with no-record for an ID no record has, 400 without an ID, and no-repo with a calm message for a folder outside any git repository.

title: The layout gives the same map every time, whatever the focus, with no overlaps
when: Builds the map of the test workspace twice.
then: Expects the same map for the same index and the same places and sizes for an index built again, no two boxes overlapping, the nav's order within a level, and a trace's picture centered on its focus.

title: git runs with an argument array, inside the product root, cut at the output cap and stopped at the time limit
then: Expects shell text in an argument to stay text, git to run at the product root, output past the cap to be cut and marked, and a zero time limit to stop it.

title: In the Graph view Details follows the node under the pointer or keyboard focus, then the page's record
then: Expects the page's record with its compact Traceability, data file and what the graph connects; a hovered node's details with "Under the pointer" and Open at its address; the page's record back on leaving, in the same box; and the same for a node with keyboard focus.

title: In the Wiki view Details shows only what the page does not: the data file and line, the columns of its row and the raw links; a focused or right-clicked record row shows that record
then: Expects the data file and line, the columns of its row and the raw links, and no children, problems or identity block; a record row with focus shows that record as "Selected" until focus leaves; a right-clicked row stays until a click elsewhere.

title: History lists the file's commits, the uncommitted change first, shows a diff inline and loads more
when: With the history API answered in the test.
then: Expects "Not committed" first and then twenty commits with date, author and short hash; the uncommitted diff inline with its removed, added and header lines marked; one diff open at a time; Load more adding the rest; and the calm message when the folder is not a git repository.

title: On a phone the side bar is a bottom sheet with the same three views
when: On a narrow screen, opens the side bar from the page bar.
then: Expects a sheet holding the "Side bar views" switcher, and Outline shown under its heading when chosen.

title: A parent spans its children stacked, an equal part each, from its top edge to its bottom edge, each child beside it, nothing overlapping
when: Builds the maps of three workspaces, two synthetic trees and a product with a busy part and a quiet one.
then: Expects every root the product box's height, every parent's children of one height, stacked from its top to its bottom a tenth of each one's part apart, each in the next level right of it, no two boxes in a level overlapping, the busy part and the quiet one the same height with the busy one's children smaller, and the tree the nav's.

title: Every box in a column has its width, a fixed fraction of the map
then: In the Tree maps of three workspaces and three synthetic trees every column 0.4 times as wide as the one before from the product's, with a gap before it of 0.15 times its width, every box in a column at its place and width, and the map as wide as its columns.

title: A parent line runs level from the parent's right edge to the child's left edge, at the child's middle
then: Expects every parent line of the map level at its child's middle, from the parent's right edge to the child's left edge, and a cross-link leaving each box on the side facing the other.

title: Tall parents carry their height and text scale, every box its text scale as its box scale, and every parent line is level
when: Opens a domain's graph at depth 2.
then: Expects, in the drawn scene, the domain taller than its stages stacked with a text scale above 1, every drawn box's box scale its text scale, and every parent line drawn level.

title: The glide is one smooth zoom and pan, from the view as it is to the framed one
then: Expects the zoom path between a domain's frame and a requirement's to start and end at those views, its zoom changing smoothly between frames, and its duration the shared speed for a short path and at most twice it for a long one.

title: The breadcrumb trail grows with each visit and cuts back on a revisit
then: Expects the trail to add new records, cut back to a record visited before, and keep only the most recent records.

title: Only boxes in view and big enough are drawn, each with its label, with bars for the rest, within a budget
when: Frames a domain.
then: Expects only boxes in view and at least 3 pixels tall, each drawn as its ID alone (its label always drawn); far out, no box too small and a bar for each run of tiny children inside its parent's span; a forced box drawn whatever its size; the same view drawing the same; and a synthetic product of more than 3,000 nodes within the budget at every zoom.

title: Every drawn box shows its label, however small on screen, and is a keyboard stop; the summary counts the framed picture
when: Opens a domain's graph at depth 3 with sixty requirements a few pixels tall.
then: Expects every drawn box to show its kind and ID line and its title, and every box in the keyboard layer to be drawn, with an accessible name, a Tab stop and not hidden from assistive technology; the keyboard order over every drawn box, column by column; and the summary counting the framed picture.

title: With Links on, links draw as curves between their boxes, and the edge hints count the linked records past each edge
then: Checks the hints' arithmetic, then turns Links on for a requirement and expects every linked record drawn wherever it is, each link a curve, and the parent lines straight and level.

title: Stability: focusing anything moves the camera only, and no box changes its place or size
when: Focuses a domain, a stage, a folder, a capability and a use case by clicking, then goes Back twice and Forward once.
then: Expects each step stable, the camera different at each, and every box seen to keep the same place and size in the map throughout.

title: A domain node has the hexagon class and its outline, and the tree lines meet that outline
then: Checks the chamfer's growth and cap, a line out of a domain starting at the point's tip at its middle and on its slanted side above it, a line into a domain meeting the tip; and on a product's graph every domain node, and only domains, carrying the hexagon's class and its polygon outline, and the product its rounded box.

title: Stability: a domain is drawn as a hexagon, its outline the polygon in every state
when: Opens the product's graph.
then: Expects the domain drawn as its hexagon, its outline a six-cornered polygon; hovered, the same polygon in the hover state; focused, still the polygon, drawn as the focus; and the product drawn as a rounded box, not a polygon.

title: A label keeps its size in the map: its text scale is the map's, and the camera never changes it
then: Checks every box's text scale is at most its column's width over 400, set by the map, and that at a quarter, one and four times a domain's framing zoom every drawn box carries no text size of its own: the camera never changes a label.

title: Stability: at depth 2 on a domain, the domain, its stages and their folders are framed in the canvas, each showing its full title wrapped on whole words
when: Opens the Exploring domain's graph at depth 2.
then: Expects, in the drawn scene, the domain, every stage and at least half the folders wholly in the canvas, and every framed box (the domain, its product at the left edge, its stages and their folders) labeled with its whole title, each of its lines fitting as drawn and every line but the last ending after a space or a hyphen.

title: A space's index holds only its product's records, links, parts, coverage and problems, and the records and problems of no product
when: With a link and a named ID from Demo shop into Notebook.
then: Expects each space's index to hold its own records, parts and those of no product, no link into the other, its own coverage, and its problems with the workspace's.

title: Each product has its own graph map
then: Expects Demo shop's map to have Demo shop as its single root and only its nodes, a record of no product to root a map of its own, and the graph with Links on to draw nothing of Notebook.

title: Clicking a node re-centers the graph and changes the address, and Back walks back
when: Renders the graph page in jsdom, clicks a neighbor.
then: Expects the address, side bar and trail to change; then goes back and expects the first record again.

title: No screen of one space shows another product: the side bar, text, the format reference and Checks
then: Expects the side bar to list no link into Notebook and Notebook's domain ID named in a text field to be plain text, the reference to count and link only the space's records, and Notebook's Checks to name nothing of Demo shop.

title: The products page is the space chooser
then: Expects one card per product with its ID, name and domain count, and no problems or coverage.

title: In the Tree map siblings share one text scale, their column's width's share or the largest at which every sibling's label fits, and every label fits its box
when: In the Tree maps of three workspaces and three synthetic trees.
then: Expects every group of siblings to share one box size and one text scale, above 0, equal to the least of their labels' largest fits within their column's width over 400 (a title with a word too wide for its column lowering its siblings' scale with its own); every label's lines to give back its title and its kind and ID line, each line's estimated width within its box's width over its scale, less the padding, its shape's room and (beside the kind and ID line) its marks and badge, no word broken, its lines and border no taller than its box, and every label centered; and that the estimate errs wide and wrapping breaks only after a space, a word too wide for a line after a hyphen (or a path after a slash) and then between characters.

title: Stability: no label is clipped, in light and dark, focused or not, at several zooms
when: In light and dark, on the Exploring domain and its Define stage at depths 1 to 3 and zoomed in twice.
then: Expects every drawn box in the canvas to fit each of its lines (each line the map broke its kind and ID line and its title into), read from the drawn scene: each line's width as the canvas measures it at its drawn font at most its placed width, and the line inside its box, with half a map unit and half a pixel to spare.

title: Stability: a label keeps its size in the map when the focus changes and the camera zooms
when: Opens the Exploring domain's graph, reads its Design stage's title font size in the drawn scene (its font on screen over the zoom) and its lines, focuses the stage and then zooms in.
then: Expects the font size in map units and the lines unchanged each time, and the title's size on screen to change only with the camera's zoom.

title: The Nested map holds each box's children below its header band, top-down from the product's fixed square, siblings equal squares
when: Lays out the test workspaces, synthetic trees and a product with a busy part and a quiet one.
then: Expects every child inside its parent's padding below the header band, siblings never overlapping, a parent before its children in the keyboard's order, and the same roots and children as the Tree map; every root the product's square, every group of siblings equal squares, and the busy part and the quiet one the same size with the busy one's children smaller.

title: Children are a grid of equal squares in the tree's order, with the column count that makes them largest
then: Expects four squares in a square room to be two by two, five in a wide room one row, three in a square room two columns with a blank cell and the gap taken off the side, no column count giving larger squares than the one chosen, and in every test map each parent's children in the tree's order, row by row, a gap apart.

title: In the Nested map siblings share one text scale and one header band, and every label fits its box
when: In every test map.
then: Expects every group of siblings to share one text scale, above 0 and at most their side over 400, equal to the least of their labels' largest fits (a leaf's in its square, a parent's in a header band a quarter of it), a word too wide for a busy part's leaves lowering their scale and their cousins' in the same part but not their parent's, and the parents among them one header band, the tallest of their labels; every label wrapped within its box's width, no word broken, its lines giving back its title, a leaf's inside its square and a parent's inside its header band; and the same map object for an index whatever the focus.

title: In the Nested view the camera frames the focus box, whatever the depth, and draws each box with its label
when: Frames a domain, a stage and a record in the Nested map on a canvas of 1000 by 800.
then: Expects the focus's box centered and within the padding, every drawn box only its ID (its label always drawn), a parent drawn before its children, nothing drawn out of view or under 3 pixels, and the drawing within its budget.

title: Stability: every graph feature works the same in the Tree, Nested and Voronoi views
when: Runs one table of the graph's features in each view.
then: The Layout switch and its `v` command, a click to focus, Enter on a focused box, Tab and arrow keys with a visible focus ring, the step keys, `.` framing the focus, depth 1 to 3, Links, a hidden kind keeping its space, the minimap, the trail, Back and Forward, the hover spotlight with Details following it, and the side bar's Outline; in the Nested view, every drawn child inside its parent's box on screen and the view kept across a reload of the tab; and in the Voronoi view, every drawn cell a polygon whose label's middle the pointer finds it at, inside its parent's box on screen.

title: In the Graph view the side bar shows kind, title, problems, gaps and a page link
when: Centers the graph on a rule with problems and gaps.
then: Expects the side bar's Details to show its kind, title and problems, its gaps in its compact Traceability, and a link to the record page.

title: Every title in Lathe's spec and the Tool Library wraps on whole words, none broken inside a word
when: Reads every record of Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library's, wraps each title as its box would (in its kind's shape's room).
then: Expects the lines to give the title back, every line but the last to end after a space or after a hyphen inside one word too wide for a line, and a component's file path to break only after a slash or a hyphen.

title: The Voronoi map holds each cell's children inside its outline, equal-area cells top-down from the product's fixed hexagon, the same every time
when: Lays out the test workspaces and synthetic trees.
then: Expects every cell convex with its node's box as its bounding box, every child's corners inside its parent's outline and below its header's cut, siblings never overlapping, a parent before its children in the keyboard's order, and the same roots and children as the Tree map; the product a flat-topped hexagon of the fixed area, as wide as the product box; at least 95% of cells within 5% of their siblings' mean area, whatever the records under them; the same tree giving an equal map, a record added under one parent leaving every cell outside it, and that parent's own, exactly in place, and one shape split the same way at any place and size; and the convex helpers insetting, cutting and crossing a square.

title: In the Voronoi map siblings share one text scale, at most their size's, and each label wraps on whole words inside its outline
then: Expects every group of sibling cells in the test maps to share one text scale, above 0 and at most the smallest sibling's square root of its area over 400; every cell's label box inside its outline, a parent's above where its children start; every title line but the last ending after a space and no line wider than the label; one map per index whatever the focus, the same map for a spec loaded again with the same tree, and the worker's layout of the tree read from the index equal to the one made here.

title: In the Voronoi view the camera frames the focus cell, and the page draws each cell as its outline
when: Frames the product, a domain and a use case in the Voronoi map on a canvas of 1000 by 800.
then: Expects the focus's box centered, every drawn cell in view and at least 3 pixels across, a parent drawn before its children, the drawing within its budget and the focus drawn. On the page, with the Voronoi layout chosen, expects each cell drawn as its polygon with its label inside, the pointer finding the cell at its label's middle and not at a corner of its bounding box outside its outline, and a click on a child gliding the camera to frame its cell.

title: Depth shows only in the Tree layout
when: Opens a stage in the Tree layout.
then: Expects the Depth buttons shown. Switches to Nested and then Voronoi, and expects the Depth group to keep its slot but be hidden, aria-hidden and inert, so it is neither seen nor reached. Switches back to Tree and expects it again.

title: An API's page lists its endpoints, with their method and route, and the requirements they share
when: Renders an API's page.
then: Expects an Endpoints section listing its endpoint with its method and route, a Shared requirements section with its requirement, and no plain Children list.

title: An integration's page lists its exchanges and names the outside system
when: Renders an integration's page.
then: Expects an Exchanges section with its count, the outside system named, and the exchange's row.

title: A technical flow reads as a step table per path, with each step's component and what it satisfies
when: Renders a technical flow with two main steps and a refused one.
then: Expects a table per path with the columns Step, What happens, Component and Satisfies, the linked IDs in each, and the step's transaction, locks and statements folded under its row.

title: An API and an integration sit in Interaction design, and a technical flow in Technical specification under its layer
when: Builds a domain's folders.
then: Expects the API and the integration in Interaction design, and the technical flow beside the component in its layer's group in Technical specification.

title: In a trace, a technical step that satisfies the rule brings its technical flow and the component it uses
when: Traces a domain rule a technical step satisfies.
then: Expects the step, its technical flow and its component in the chain, joined by their links, with the step's column before the component's.

title: Nodes and lines show stage, relation, errors and gaps, with a legend
then: Expects each node drawn in its stage's colors, an error badge on a test with an error and none on a clean view, a gap badge on a rule with a gap, the lines' relation families, and a legend.

title: Requirements, pattern rules and standard rules read under their group headings, the ungrouped first, and the Outline lists the groups
when: Opens a use case with one ungrouped requirement and three in two groups (one written in another case).
then: Expects the Children section and the requirement table to show the ungrouped one first and each group under its heading, the Outline to list the groups, a pattern page to group its rules the same way, and a standard's rule table to head its group's rows.

title: Every kind is drawn in its own shape, a group as a folder and a kind a product adds as a plain box, each shape keeping its label and badge clear of its notches and corners at every size, and the key shows every shape and mark
then: Expects every kind of the meta-model to have the shape and mark of the rule's table, a group a folder and an unknown kind a plain box, every shape and mark used and named in the key; on a leaf and on boxes grown with their level, a label as tall and wide as its padding and room allow, and its badge at the top right, inside every shape's outline; and each shape's outline, notch and room as the page draws them.

title: Stability: in the Tree view every label line and badge sits inside its box's shape, and in the Nested view every record shows its shape's mark
when: Opens a domain's graph in the Tree view at each depth, and for every drawn box big enough to read hit-tests, with the canvas's own hit test, the corners of each label line (at its drawn width) and each badge, expecting each to land on its own box, inside its polygon or rounded outline; then in the Nested view.
then: Expects every record box to be drawn with its kind's shape mark and no outline of its own.

title: A framed box's header reads at the same size on screen at every depth, and the camera can frame the deepest leaf
when: Loads the repo's own specs (Lathe and the Tool Library) and, in each layout, frames every box at depth 1 in a 770 by 640 pane with the real camera.
then: Expects every frame within the camera's zoom limits; the framed title's median size on screen at each depth exactly the same at every depth in Nested and in the Tree (of each parent but the product whose text its column sets and whose frame its columns' width sets), within 40% across depths in Voronoi, and between 9 and 20 pixels; and the smallest box of each map framed short of the zoom limit.

title: Arrow keys move between nodes, Enter re-centers and Escape clears filters
when: Focuses the center node, moves with the arrow keys, presses Enter.
then: Expects the graph to re-center with focus on the new center; then hides a kind and expects Escape to show it again.

title: Each label line is placed in map units at its face's size times its box's text scale, inside its box, and drawn at that size times the zoom
when: For every box of the Tree, Nested and Voronoi maps of the test workspace.
then: Expects each label line's size to be its face's at text scale 1 times the box's text scale, and the whole line inside its box (a cell's inside its polygon), and every badge inside its box. On the page, expects each drawn line's font on screen to be its map size times the zoom, and a line under `TEXT_BAR_PX` drawn as a bar. Expects the canvas's measure to read each width once at its face's font, and the plain measure to be the same every time.

title: The pointer finds the deepest box under it from the map's outlines
then: Expects a point inside a polygon found and one outside not; a rounded box's corner outside its curve not its box; in each layout the middle of every box's label to find that box, not its parent drawn under it; nothing far outside the map; and a hexagon's cut corner outside the domain.

title: Only boxes on screen are drawn, placed relative to the camera's center
then: Expects a box on screen drawn and a box wholly past an edge culled, a far box coming into view when the camera zooms out about the same center, and a tiny box deep in a very large map, at a very deep zoom, placed as exactly as one near the origin.

title: Opens a form of typed inputs, writes only what changed, and shows the record changed
key: opens a form of typed inputs, writes only what changed, and shows the record changed
when: Opens a requirement's page, chooses Edit, changes its statement and group, and saves.
then: Expects a form of typed inputs in place of the page's content, one write with only the changed columns, and the page showing the record changed.

title: Adds a child from its parent's page with a suggested ID, and opens it
key: with a suggested ID, and opens it
when: On a use case's page chooses Add requirement, fills the form and saves.
then: Expects an empty form with the parent set and the next free ID suggested, one write that adds the record, and the new record's page opened.

title: Asks first, naming what still references the record, and shows the store's refusal inline
key: asks first, naming what still references the record
when: Chooses Remove on a record that others reference, and confirms.
then: Expects a question that lists the children and links that name it before anything is written, and the store's refusal shown inline after the write.

title: Shows the store's refusal inline, at the top and beside the part of the form it came from, and keeps the draft
key: refusal inline, at the top and beside the part of the form it came from, and keeps the draft
when: Saves a change the store refuses.
then: Expects the form still open with what was entered, every reason at its top and beside the input its command came from, and the page unchanged.

title: Edit a record with the keyboard, and focus comes back to its actions
key: edit a record with the keyboard, and focus comes back to its actions
when: In Chromium, opens a record, reaches Edit by Tab, changes a field and saves with the keyboard alone, with axe-core run on the form.
then: Expects focus on the form's first input, the save done from the keyboard, focus back on the record's actions, and no axe-core finding at WCAG 2.2 AA.

title: Open the form, save an edit
key: open the form, save an edit
when: In Chromium, over a copy of a product, opens a record, chooses Edit, changes a field and saves.
then: Expects the form in place of the content, the record shown changed after the write, and nothing on the page jumping.

title: Add a child from its parent's page
key: add a child from its parent
when: In Chromium, over a copy of a product, adds a child from its parent's page.
then: Expects the new record written and opened, and nothing on the page jumping.

title: Record, domain and product pages show the graph in their Graph view, and the nav has no Graph item
when: Opens a record page, a domain page and a product page.
then: Expects no Graph item in the nav, and expects each page's Graph view to show its graph at the right address.

title: Ask to remove a referenced record, and see the refusal
key: ask to remove a referenced record, and see the refusal
when: In Chromium, chooses Remove on a record others reference, and confirms.
then: Expects the question naming what references it, the store's refusal shown inline, and the record kept.

title: Gives every column but the ID and the parent columns a typed input, in the table's order
key: gives every column but the ID and the parent columns a typed input
when: Builds the form fields of several kinds from a schema description.
then: Expects one input per column in the table's order, typed by the column: a select for an enum, a number for a whole number, a check for true or false, a date, a list, with required columns marked.

title: Offers as parents and link targets only records of the allowed kinds in the same product
key: offers as parents only records of the allowed parent kinds in the same product
when: Asks for a record's parent choices and the targets of the links its kind may start.
then: Expects only records of the allowed kinds, in the record's product, never the record's own subtree as a parent.

title: Suggests the next free number in the kind's convention, and fills a new record's parent columns
key: suggests the next free number in the kind
when: Asks for an ID for a new record under several parents.
then: Expects the next free number in the kind's ID convention, or the start of a named ID.

title: Names what still references the record, and what goes with it, before a removal
key: names what still references the record, and what goes with it
when: Asks what a removal of a referenced record would meet.
then: Expects its children and the links into it listed as what refuses the removal, and its parts and own links as what goes with it.

title: Changes only what changed: the columns set or cleared, a move, links taken and added, and a part table written again
key: changes only what changed
when: Turns an edited draft into commands.
then: Expects one write holding only a set of the changed columns, a move when the parent changed, the links taken and added, and the part rows written again.

title: Columns follow the parent/child tree, and a trace has its own columns
then: Expects a requirement's ancestors in columns 0 to 3, the domain's other children beside the use case whatever their kind, every parent line running from one column to the next, and trace columns from the rule to the files, with a kind a product adds placed with the components.

title: The graph reads left to right by column, and so does a trace
then: Expects one x and one width per level of the map, levels left to right a gap apart, ancestors to the left of a record, and a trace's columns from the requirement to its files.

title: Links between records in one column are drawn but never change the map
when: Adds two aggregates that link to each other.
then: Expects them in one column with both links in the picture, and every box of the map where it was without the links.

title: The page draws the map in columns with a solid parent/child spine, and links between siblings never move anything
when: Opens a requirement's graph with Links on.
then: Expects the use case left of the requirement, the component and the test that link to it at their own places in the map, and a solid spine; then two sibling aggregates that link to each other, in one column, with both links drawn between them.

title: A record with several kinds of child has a labeled, counted group per kind
then: Checks which records are grouped (only those with more than one kind of child, however many of one kind), the groups' labels such as "Requirements (6)", their members, and that a group's ID is its parent and kind and names no record.

title: Every group is in the map with all its members beside it, and the spine runs record, group, record
when: Frames a domain at depths 1 and 2.
then: Expects its stages and folders as groups with their counts, the spine running through a group to its records, every group in the map holding all its members right beside it and spanning them exactly, and cross-links running record to record.

title: A group can be the focus: its parent and all its members are shown, and depth counts levels from it
when: Centers on the Capabilities folder.
then: Expects its stage and every member, the spine through it, the members' children and groups framed at depth 2 and their members at depth 3, nothing for a group that does not exist, an older kind group's address still working, and its `/<domain-id>/<stage>/<folder>` address both ways, the old `/graph/...` one leading there.

title: Groups take their own column between the parent and its children
when: Lays out a group's neighborhood.
then: Expects the parent, the group, its members, a member's own group and its members from left to right, a member's group beside another member's ungrouped child, and every group one column after its parent and one before its members.

title: A group carries a summary mark for problems and gaps beneath it
then: Expects the aggregates' group to carry the warnings and gaps of the rules beneath the aggregate, the tests' group to carry the test's error, and the use cases' group nothing.

title: Trace mode has no groups, and filters hide groups with their kind or the parent relation
then: Expects no groups in a trace, no group for a hidden kind, no groups at all when parent/child is hidden, and the same graph every time.

title: A group shows its name and count, with no chevron; clicking a group, or Enter on it, goes to it
when: Opens a domain's graph.
then: Expects the open questions' group drawn as a folder with no chevron and no button; clicks the group and expects its address, the group the center, and its name and count in its tooltip; goes back and presses Enter on a stage and expects its address.

title: A group has its own address with its parent left and its members right, and Back works
when: Follows the domain panel's link to a group.
then: Expects the group's address, panel, columns and trail (the domain as "Domain (P-D)", the group as "Use cases" with its parent in the tooltip), follows a member and goes Back to the group; then expects a message for a group that does not exist.

title: Groups are drawn as folders with marks for trouble beneath them, and the legend explains them
when: Renders a domain.
then: Expects error and gap marks on the groups with trouble beneath them, none on a clean group, an accessible label that says folded, and a legend entry for groups.

title: The graph is a component that reports moves through a callback and fits a resized container
when: Renders the graph view on its own with a callback and its own link addresses, clicks a node and a panel link.
then: Expects the callback, not an address change; then resizes its container and expects the picture fitted again.

title: A record and a group each have one address, in every view
when: Parses record and group addresses at their bare IDs, builds the address of a record, a group and a domain.
then: Expects `?view=split` to name no view, then opens a record in the Graph view at its ID and a group page at its own address.

title: The view toggles open and close panes, at least one stays open, and the open views are remembered and named in the link
when: Opens a record with the wiki alone.
then: Expects no Split or Open beside, clicks Wiki and expects it to stay open with a tooltip that says why, opens the graph beside it and expects `?view=wiki,graph` and the panes in order, closes the wiki, opens another record and expects the graph again, then opens `?view=wiki,graph` and expects the wiki and the graph, remembered as `wiki,graph`, with the View toggles once, in the page bar.

title: Both panes follow one focus, Back moves both, and graph settings survive
when: With the wiki and graph open, follows a child link in the wiki.
then: Expects the graph re-centered, clicks a node and expects the wiki and title to follow, goes Back and expects both to return, and expects depth 2 kept across pages and a trip to the Wiki view.

title: A group page shows its parent, kind and members with their marks
when: Opens a group of domain rules.
then: Expects the parent link, the kind's description, and each member with its gap marks and problem badge.

title: Product and domain pages have the views, the graph centered on them
when: Opens a product and a domain with the wiki and graph open.
then: Expects a wiki pane and a graph centered on the product or domain.

title: Lists in the side bar and on group pages stay at ten rows
when: Gives a use case 13 requirements.
then: Expects search boxes on the group page's members, the side bar's connected records, and the side bar's Outline of the graph's levels.

title: The nav collapses to a rail with tooltips, remembered
when: Collapses the nav.
then: Expects the rail's icons with names and tooltips and the choice remembered on the next page, then opens it again from the rail.

title: On a narrow screen the nav is a full-screen sheet
when: With a narrow screen, opens the nav sheet from the menu button.
then: Expects focus in quick find, closes it with Escape (focus back on the button), with a click outside, and by choosing a page.

title: Nav sections fold, the current place opens and is marked, with badges and a footer
then: Expects no heading for the current space, its overview first, folds a section, opens a page in a folded section and expects it open, opens a domain page and expects it marked current, and checks the tooltip on a long name, the Checks badges and the footer.

title: Quick find ranks matches and opens one with the keyboard
when: Ranks records and domains by ID and title, then types in quick find, moves down with the arrow key and opens the second result with Enter.

title: The side bar shows the record in the Graph view and folds away, remembered per view mode
then: Expects the side bar open in a record's Graph view with the record and what the graph connects, hides it with its own button, expects the main view to take the space and the choice remembered in the Graph view of another record, shows it again and expects that record, and expects the Wiki view still closed, its own choice.

title: On a narrow screen the side bar is a bottom sheet
when: With a narrow screen, opens the side bar from the page bar.
then: Expects a bottom sheet with focus inside, closes it with Escape and expects focus back on the toggle.

title: Folded rows keep counts and marks and open by button, Expand all or arrow keys, remembered
when: On a domain page.
then: Expects use cases and aggregates folded with their counts, opens and closes a row by button and by the arrow keys (moving into it and back to its parent), uses Expand all, and expects open rows still open after visiting another page.

title: Record and product pages show one level, and the side bar does not repeat it
when: Opens a domain's page.
then: Expects its records listed in their folders with their children folded, a record page whose wiki lists its children while the side bar does not, and a product page that lists its domains but none of their records.

title: Switching views by keyboard keeps focus, and the toggles show a focus ring
when: Focuses a button in the graph pane, closes the graph with Ctrl+2.
then: Expects focus on the Graph toggle, now in the wiki pane's bar; checks the toggle tooltips (Alt+G off a Mac) and the focus ring style.

title: Every record ID named in the text becomes a link to its record, with its title on hover
when: Renders a text field.
then: Expects every occurrence of each named record ID linked to its record page with its title on hover.

title: IDs in code blocks, code with other text, links and longer IDs are not linked; a lone-ID code span is
then: Expects no links for IDs in code blocks, code spans with other text, links or longer IDs, a link around a code span holding one lone ID, and HTML left unchanged when there is nothing to link.

title: Only the IDs of records are linked, never the record itself; an ID that is no record is not
then: Expects a text field's links to be the records of the space it names, without the record's own ID, and an ID that is no record left as plain text.

title: On a record page a text field links the records it names, leaves an unknown ID as text, and a link moves within the app
when: Opens a record page.
then: Expects the named records as links, an unknown ID as plain text, code left plain, and a click that moves to the record.

title: An ID inside a longer ID links only as the longer one, a named record is not a link between records, and domain pages link theirs too
then: Expects only the named ID linked beside a longer ID, no such link in the side bar or the graph, and a domain overview that links the records its text names.

title: Pattern rules sit under their pattern in the graph
then: Expects parent lines from the pattern to its rules and each rule one column to the pattern's right.

title: Follows is drawn as a cross-link
then: Expects follows lines shown and styled as pattern links, and each use case reached from the pattern by one sitting a column after it, the link laid out pointing right.

title: Trace mode for a pattern rule
then: Expects trace mode offered for a pattern rule, not a pattern, with what satisfies and proves it in every domain.

title: A pattern's Graph view draws its rules and follows lines
when: Opens a pattern in the Graph view.
then: Expects its rules drawn, a follows line in the pattern style, and the legend naming it.

title: The nav has no Graph item and the graph stays a view away
then: Expects no Graph item in the open nav or the rail, the page's Graph view, Ctrl+2 and the palette's Graph view command.

title: A flow page shows its steps in order as a table
when: Opens a flow with three steps written out of order.
then: Expects the Steps table with its four columns (Step, What happens, Uses, Carries out), rows in step order, and each cell linking the IDs.

title: Each step's description and the titles of what it uses and fulfills are folded under its row
then: Expects a step's description hidden until its row is unfolded, then rendered with the titles and kinds of what it fulfills; Expand all and Collapse all open and close every row.

title: A step row carries its problems, and a flow without steps has no table
then: Expects a warning badge on a step's row, and no Steps section on a flow without steps.

title: Steps are ordered by their position as a number, then by ID
then: Expects `stepsOf` to order steps 2 then 10, and two steps of one position by ID.

title: A flow step sits one column right of its flow, joined by the parent line
then: Expects a flow's three steps in its neighborhood, joined to it directly, all in the column after it.

title: A flow's steps hang under it directly, or through a group beside other kinds
then: Expects a flow with six steps and nothing else to reach them directly, and one that also has an interaction requirement to reach them through a "Flow steps (6)" group in the next column, its steps framed at depth 2, and in the map each step under the group and the group under the flow.

title: A requirement's trace shows the fulfilling step, its flow and the components it uses
then: Expects the trace of a requirement to hold the step that fulfills it, its flow and the component it uses, in that column order, still laid out in columns.

title: The rail lists the products in order with their icons or monograms
then: Checks the icon and color fields and the monogram, then expects three products in ID order with a monogram, a monogram for an icon too long, an emoji icon, and nothing after them.

title: The current space is the page's product and is marked
then: Expects the product of product, domain, record, group and Checks pages and none for the products and the format, the mark and accent bar on the current space, and the space kept on its Checks page.

title: Choosing a space scopes the nav to its domains, folders and groups
then: Expects the current space's domains; unfolding a domain, then Define, then Use cases shows its capabilities in order before the use cases outside any capability. Expects the product's groups and none of another product's; choosing another space swaps them.

title: Choosing a space opens its last page this session
when: Moves between two spaces.
then: Expects each to reopen the page left in it, remembered in session storage only.

title: Alt and a number switch spaces, and the palette has Switch to commands
when: From the products page, presses Alt+3 and Alt+1.
then: Expects a number with no space left alone and Ctrl+Shift+M still opening the space's Checks, and runs a Switch to command from the palette.

title: Quick find searches the current space only
then: Expects only the current space's records among the matches, none of another product's and no groups, walked as one list.

title: Each space has its own Checks page
when: Opens.
then: Checks from the nav in Notebook and in Demo shop and expects each at its product's address with only its own problems, then the workspace's under Workspace, and no filter.

title: The rail stays in the narrow-screen drawer
when: On a narrow screen, opens the nav sheet.
then: Expects the rail, and switches space from it.

title: Siblings of mixed kinds share a column
then: Expects a component's sibling groups in one column and their members of several kinds in the next, every node with the same parent in one column, and a domain's open groups' members of eight kinds at one x position on the canvas.

title: Ancestors sit to the left of the focus and descendants to its right
then: Expects a use case's product, domain and group in columns 0 to 2, the use case in column 3 and its requirement in column 4, and the same order on the canvas.

title: A cross-linked record sits one column after its source
when: With parent lines hidden.
then: Expects a view one column after the requirement it fulfills and an endpoint one after the view; expects a test one column after the requirement it proves, unless the domain is shown, when it sits beside the use case as the domain's child.

title: A group sits in its own column between its parent and its members
then: Expects a domain, its use case group, the use cases, a use case's requirement group and its opened members each one column further right, the group beside another use case's ungrouped requirement.

title: Within a column nodes follow their parent's place, then the nav's order, and keep it when the graph re-centers
then: Expects use cases by ID, their children in their parents' order, a domain's groups in kind order, rows numbered from 0 and drawn top to bottom, and the same order after re-centring.

title: Trace mode keeps its own columns
then: Expects every node of a requirement's trace in its kind's trace column, the requirement in column 0.

title: Domains fold into Define, Design and Open questions, one level at a time, with counts
then: Expects the space's domains folded by default; a domain opening into Define, Design and Open questions with counts; each stage opening into its folders, still folded; and a folder listing its records.

title: A stage or folder with no records is left out of the nav
then: Expects a domain with only a use case to show Define with only Use cases, and no Design.

title: The current page's branch opens itself
then: Expects a requirement's page to open its use case's folder, a component's page Technical specification with the component marked, a group page its kind's folder and its eyebrow to name Design › Interaction design, and a domain page its domain.

title: Folder names and order come from the schema sections, in the nav and on the domain page alike
then: Expects a renamed and reordered folder to show with its new name and place in both the nav and the domain page's headings.

title: The product shows Shared only when it has patterns
then: Expects Shared with the product's pattern, no Patterns group, a pattern rule's page opening Shared, and no Shared for a product without patterns.

title: A capability's flows and tests sit in their folders, its use cases under it
then: Expects each folder's records, with a capability's flow and test lifted into Interaction design and Test plan; the domain page's Use cases headed Capabilities, then Use cases outside any capability; and a capability's use case opening its capability's branch.

title: A kind in no known folder gets a folder of its own
then: Expects a Define kind with no folder at the end of Define, a kind of no stage after the stages, and each kind's folder path.

title: What is folded is remembered for the session, and every record is listed without sections
then: Expects open rows to stay open on another page, kept in session storage only, and, without sections, one folder per kind under its stage.

title: At depth 1 the graph frames the tree around the focus: its parent or folder at the left edge, its children or their folders, and no other links
when: Frames a use case in a folder, a domain, a use case with two kinds of children and a requirement at depth 1.
then: Expects the parent, the children or their groups, no siblings, and only parent lines.

title: The graph opens at depth 1, framing the parent and the children; depth 2 and 3 frame more levels below, and Links brings in the links
when: Opens the Define stage's graph.
then: Expects the depth buttons 1 to 3 with 1 pressed and no links, then depth 2 framing more records with a new summary; then a requirement's graph with Links on, its linked view and test drawn and a dashed link.

title: Technical specification lists layers in order, each with its components, then those outside any layer
then: Expects three layers whose order is not their ID order in their order, each with its components, then "Components outside any layer", the folder counting components; and a domain with no layers listing its components directly.

title: Test plan puts each test in one group by family, then by what it proves, empty groups left out
then: Expects tests in the seven groups (acceptance, domain rule, pattern, interaction, UI, design and engineering): a capability's test in Acceptance within its capability, acceptance tests by capability in order and by the first use case each proves, a test proving two kinds in the first group, a view's interaction requirement and `test_type` `ui` in UI tests, `test_type` `design` and a test with only `supports` links in Design checks, no empty groups, and no group level when only one group has tests.

title: In the nav, layers link and fold, test groups only fold, all with counts
then: Expects the Design folders' counts, Technical specification's layers folded with counts and links to their pages, a layer opening into its components, and Test plan's groups as buttons with no links, opening down to a use case's tests.

title: The current page's branch opens through its layer or its test groups
then: Expects the branch keys of a component, a layer, a component outside any layer and an acceptance test, and the nav opening a component's layer, a layer's own row and a domain rule test's group when their pages open.

title: The domain page heads the same layers and test groups, layers linking to their pages
then: Expects the layers and test groups as h4 to h6 headings in the nav's order, layer headings linking to their pages and test group headings not, rows still folded one level deep, and the filter keeping only groups that hold a match.

title: A layer's record page lists its components as its children
then: Expects a layer's page to name its product, domain and kind, and list its two components under Children.

title: A product's lathe.config.json chooses the data folder
when: Loads a folder whose config names `docs/data`, with a stray `data/` folder at the root.
then: Expects only the records of `docs/data` read, with no problems, and the root `data/` ignored.

title: A product's own kinds and relations add tables to the schema
when: Loads a fixture whose data declares a `report` kind and a `summarizes` relation as `product_kind` and `product_relation` rows.
then: Expects the `report` kind among the kinds, a report record under its domain, the `summarizes` relation and its link, and no errors.

title: loadWorkspace returns the Workspace contract
when: Loads a fixture.
then: Expects exactly the fields of `Workspace` and its parts in `lathe/src/types.ts`, including the built coverage counts, as plain JSON.

title: Each record's product and domain come from its parents, and refused data is a data-refused error
then: Expects each record of the good fixture to carry its product, domain and parent; then, with two layers made each other's parent in the data file, expects no records and only `data-refused` errors, one naming the cycle.

title: Each load reads the files afresh and writes nothing
when: Loads a copy of a fixture, changes a use case's title through the store, and loads again.
then: Expects the second load to show the change, the first result untouched, and the folder to hold no new files after either load.

title: Init writes a config and a first product record through the store, and refuses bad or repeated input
when: Runs `lathe init` in a new folder, again in the same folder, with bad or missing options, and in a folder whose config names another data folder.
then: Expects `lathe.config.json` with `{ "data": "data" }` and the product's row in `data/product.jsonl` that passes `lathe check`; a second init refused with exit 2 and the row unchanged; an invalid or missing prefix or name refused with nothing written; and an existing config kept, with the product written to its data folder.

title: Serve serves the app, the spec API and change events for the product repo
when: Starts `serve` on port 5340 for a copy of a fixture, using the built app (the package's `dist/app`, or else a build into a temporary folder).
then: Expects the app page and its script, client-side routes, `/api/spec` from the engine, and a `spec:changed` event on `/api/events` after a data file changes. Skipped with a message only when the app's packages are not installed.

title: Loading Lathe's spec takes under 2 s and a live reload under 500 ms
when: `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf`. Loads a copy of Lathe's data cold, then changes one row through the store and reloads.
then: Expects the median cold load under 2 s and the median reload under 500 ms; measures a synthetic product of about 10,000 records and the reference without a budget. On a busy machine (a one-minute load average above 12) it judges nothing and exits 3.

title: A reload after a write gives the same workspace as a fresh load, with each phase timed
when: Loads a copy of a fixture twice, changes one row through the store and loads again; builds the reference twice, declares a product kind and builds it again.
then: Expects every phase timed (open, files, checks, coverage, total), the same workspace when nothing changed, the change after the write as a fresh load gives it, and the reference to be the same object until a data file it reads changes, then to hold the new kind.

title: A config with an unknown setting is refused and names it
then: Expects a config that names a setting Lathe does not know, such as `diagrams`, refused by `loadConfig` and by `loadWorkspace` with a message naming it; the settings that went with the Markdown files (`specs`, `checks`, `metaExtensions`) refused as unknown too; and `data` naming the data folder.

title: Accessibility: focus after a move, and back on the opener when a dialog or a sheet closes
then: Expects focus to stay on the page after quick find opens a record, to stay on a view toggle and the side bar toggle after they are pressed, and to follow the box that became the graph's center. Opens the palette, the shortcuts sheet and the theme picker, expects focus inside each and Tab to stay inside, and expects focus back on the opener when each closes; at 375 px does the same for the nav drawer and the side bar sheet.

title: The graph's trail is a Tab stop only while it overflows
when: Opens a record in the Graph view.
then: Expects the trail's list to take no Tab stop while it fits, since its links are the stops. Then makes the list wider than its box, re-centers, and expects the list to become a Tab stop so the keyboard can scroll it.

title: At 1024 px with three panes and the side bar open, no two panels overlap
when: Opens an aggregate with the Wiki, Graph and Model panes and the side bar in a 1024 by 700 window, too narrow for every pane's least width beside the side bar.
then: Expects the nav, each pane and the side bar to sit left to right, each starting where the one before ends, with the side bar inside the window. Before the fix, the Graph pane ran under the side bar.

title: An old address is no page: /records, /specs and /graph addresses say so, and the address stays as typed
when: Opens `/records/<id>`, `/records/<parent>/<kind>`, `/specs`, `/specs/<product>/<domain>`, `/graph` and `/graph/<id>`.
then: Expects each to read as a missing page, to say there is no such page, and to keep its address. Then opens a record with `?view=split` and expects no Graph pane, as `split` names no view.

title: Changes are hard cutovers: no redirect, alias, legacy path or second addressOf signature in the app or the engine
when: Reads every source file in `app/src` and `lathe/src`.
then: Expects no line that says legacy, redirect or alias, naming the file and line of each, and exactly one declaration of `addressOf`, taking the ID alone.

title: Tabs and space pages saved at anything but a page's address are dropped, not converted
when: Saves a tab set with two tabs at bare IDs and two under `/records` and `/specs`, and a space's last page under `/specs`, opens the app.
then: Expects only the two tabs at bare IDs, written back that way, and the space's rail link at its product.

title: A folder opens only when it holds lathe.config.json or a data folder
when: Builds folders with a config, with only `data/`, with neither, with a broken config, and a plain file.
then: Checks which open and with which data folder, and what the refusals say; then checks the window title from the rows of `data/product.jsonl`.

title: The recent folders list puts the latest first, each folder once, at most 10
when: Adds folders to the list, adds one again, adds twelve, and reads saved lists with junk in them.

title: Each folder window reopens where it was left, and always on a screen
when: Saves windows for several folders, then places them against one or two screens.
then: Back where they were, centered when off every screen, shrunk to the largest screen, and never below the minimum size.

title: In development the window uses the 5199 server only when it answers for the opened folder
when: Chooses the development source against a fake 5199 that answers for the folder, for another folder, without the header, with an error, or not at all.
then: Checks that a free port is never 5199 or a port in use.

title: The native menus offer the app commands, by command ID, without taking any key
when: Builds the menu template for a Mac and elsewhere.
then: Checks its menus and items, that Open Recent opens the folder chosen, that every app command item sends its ID and has no accelerator, and that each command and binding is one in the app's keymap (`app/src/shell/keymap.ts`), pressed as the keymap reads it.

title: The desktop app opens a product folder in a window, bridges only window.latheDesktop and runs a menu command
then: Checks the built icons (the `.icns`, the `.ico`, each Linux size and the DEV variant). Then runs the real shell, hidden, on a temporary product folder with `serve()` from the built package and a throwaway user data folder: checks that the launch view said "Opening Smoke Shop…" before the page loaded and lifted once it had its specs, that the Dock icon is the 1024 px app icon, that the page shows the product's name, that `GET /api/spec` answered 200 (so DuckDB loads in Electron), the window's title, that the page has `window.latheDesktop` with only its ten members and no Node, that the window has a hidden title bar (`titleBarStyle`) and the page draws its own 38 px bar with its controls, that the page sent its theme's chrome colors and the main process applied them, that Help › Keyboard Shortcuts opens the shortcuts sheet, and that the folder went into the recent list. It runs only on macOS, since Electron on Linux CI needs a display server. It turns off macOS window restoration for the unpacked Electron first, asks a run that hangs to quit through its stdin before SIGTERM and then SIGKILL, and leaves no Electron running.

title: A day with the desktop app
when:
1. Run `npm --prefix desktop start`. Lathe's repo opens in a window with no white flash, in light and in dark appearance.
2. Press Cmd+O and choose a folder with neither `lathe.config.json` nor `data/`: a message says what is missing and no window opens. Choose another product's folder: a second window opens.
3. Choose File › Open Recent › Lathe's folder: the first window comes forward; no third window opens.
4. Click a link to an outside site in a record: it opens in the system browser, and the window stays on Lathe.
5. Move and resize the window, quit with Cmd+Q, and run `npm --prefix desktop start` again: the last folder opened reopens in its saved place.
6. Close every window, then run `ps -A | grep vite`: no dev server the shell started is left.
then: It passes when every step behaves as written.
notes: Manual because it watches what only a person at the screen sees: a flash, the Dock and real windows. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`.

title: Iterating on Lathe in the desktop app
when:
1. With the owner's dev server running (`npm --prefix app run dev`), run `npm --prefix desktop run dev`. The terminal says Lathe's folder comes "from shared dev server at http://localhost:5199".
2. Change a style in `app/src/styles.css`: the window updates without reloading, as the browser does.
3. Open another product folder with Cmd+O: the terminal says it comes "from own dev server" on a port other than 5199.
4. Change a record's title in that folder, on its page or with `lathe set`: the page shows the new title within a second or two. Do the same in a window started with `npm --prefix desktop start`.
5. Change a comment in `desktop/src/menu.ts`: the terminal says it restarts Electron, and the windows come back. Break the file's syntax: the build fails and the running shell stays.
6. Run `npm --prefix desktop run pack`: `desktop/release/mac-arm64/Lathe.app` (or `mac` on Intel) is built, the log says code signing was skipped, and the app opens from Finder with the chuck icon (right-click › Open the first time, since it is unsigned).
then: It passes when every step behaves as written.
notes: Manual because it changes files while the shell runs and builds the app. Run it after changing `desktop/scripts/` or the servers.

title: A menu choice sent by ID runs the app command
when: Stands in for the preload's `onCommand`, sends `toggleSideBar` twice and an unknown ID.
then: Expects the side bar hidden and shown again and nothing else to happen, then expects the app to stop listening when it unmounts.

title: Each platform's window has no system title bar, with its controls over the app's own 38 px bar
when: Builds the window options for macOS, Windows and Linux.
then: A hidden title bar everywhere, the traffic lights centered in 38 px on macOS with no overlay, and elsewhere an overlay of the shell and ink colors, 38 px high.

title: The main process applies only valid theme colors to a window's chrome
when: Applies a valid chrome to a stand-in window.
then: Expects its background set, and off a Mac its overlay; then sends names, alpha colors, `rgb()`, injected text, numbers, missing and extra keys, and expects each refused with nothing changed.

title: The title bar is drawn only in the desktop app, with room for the window's controls on each platform
when: Opens a record without `window.latheDesktop`.
then: Expects no title bar; then with it, on macOS and on Windows, and expects the bar above the app shell with the platform's room for the window's controls.

title: Back and forward follow the app's history and are disabled at its ends
when: Stands in for the Navigation API.
then: With no page either way both buttons are disabled; as pages are added behind and ahead, each enables and its click goes back or forward in the history.

title: The command center names the page and opens quick find
when: Opens a record.
then: Expects the command center to read "Lathe — " and the record's heading, and a click on it to put focus in quick find.

title: The server sends spec:changed when a data file, or the package's own data or schema, change
when: Runs the dev API plugin against a stand-in Vite server.
then: Checks which event each changed file sends: data files, Lathe's own check rows and schema send `spec:changed`, other files nothing.

title: The layout toggles run the navigation and side bar commands and show whether each panel shows
when: Clicks the navigation toggle twice and the side bar toggle twice.
then: Expects the nav to collapse and expand and the side bar to hide and show, with each toggle's `aria-pressed` following.

title: The window's chrome follows the theme
when: Stands in for `setChrome`, opens the app.
then: Expects the Lathe theme's shell and ink; then chooses Midnight and expects its shell, every color an opaque `#rrggbb`.

title: The title bar in a real window
when:
1. Run `npm --prefix desktop start`. The window has no system title bar; the traffic lights sit centered in Lathe's bar, clear of the back button.
2. Drag the bar between its controls: the window moves. Double-click it there: the window zooms (or minimizes, if the system's setting says so). Click each control: it acts and the window does not move.
3. Narrow the window: the command center shortens with an ellipsis and stays centered on the window.
4. Choose another theme and switch between light and dark: the bar and the window's background follow, with no flash.
then: It passes when every step behaves as written.
notes: Manual because it watches the window's own controls and the system's gestures, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/chrome.ts` or `app/src/shell/DesktopTitleBar.tsx`.

title: The Dock badge counts the focused product's check errors, and the Dock menu opens a new window
then: Checks the badge text from 0 to over 999, that it follows the focused window or the one focused last and a new count after a reload, that only whole counts from 0 up are taken, and that New Window runs Open Product Folder.

title: A second launch or a folder from Finder goes to the running app, which opens or focuses its window
when: Reads the folder from unpacked and packed command lines, routes a second launch to open its folder (relative to where it was launched) or to bring the app forward, routes a folder from Finder now or once ready, and finds an open folder's window however its path is spelled.

title: The launch view names the product, and the error page says what failed and offers Retry, another folder and the folder itself
when: Builds the launch view and the error page models, steps from the page's `data-specs`, reads the engine's message from the spec API's answer, runs only the buttons a page shows, and builds the About model with its versions and two links.

title: The app menu has About and Settings, File chooses the editor, and View has the record tabs
then: Checks About Lathe and Settings… (Cmd+,) in the app menu on macOS and in File and Help elsewhere, with no Check for Updates; File › Open Records In with the current editor checked; and View › Tabs, with Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab owned by the menu and every tab command sent by ID.

title: The app opts out of macOS window restoration, so a killed run leaves nothing to reopen
then: Expects `ApplePersistenceIgnoreState` YES and `NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows` NO set on macOS and nothing elsewhere, and the same defaults written for the unpacked Electron by a test harness.

title: A native Mac app at the screen
when:
1. Run `npm --prefix desktop run dev`: the Dock shows the icon with a DEV band. Run `npm --prefix desktop run pack` and open the app from `desktop/release/`: the icon is crisp in the Dock, in Finder's list view (16 px) and in Cmd+Tab, in light and in dark appearance.
2. Open a folder whose checks report errors: the Dock badge shows their number. Fix one: the badge follows. Bring a window with no errors forward: the badge clears.
3. Right-click the Dock icon: New Window opens the folder picker, and the recent folders are listed (packed app).
4. Choose Lathe › About Lathe: a small window shows the versions; Source Code and Reference open in the browser. Press Cmd+,: the focused window shows Settings.
5. On a record, click Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID in its facts, and right-click a record row, a graph node and the page title: the native menu offers the same three and each works.
6. With the app running, run `open -a Lathe ~/some/product` (packed app) or drag a product folder onto the Dock icon: the running app opens it, and a second time brings its window forward.
7. Open a new folder: the window shows the shell color and "Opening <product>…" at once, never white. Break a row of one of its data files and reopen the folder: the error page shows the message; fix it and click Retry.
8. Scroll a long page: the scroll bars float over it. Right-click in quick find: Cut, Copy and Paste. Enter full screen, quit and reopen: the window comes back in full screen, and the title bar's back button sits at the left edge.
9. Force quit Lathe while it opens its window, then open it again: macOS does not ask to reopen windows.
then: It passes when every step behaves as written. The nav keeps the theme's own color: the system's sidebar material was left out, since it needs a transparent window and nav, which would replace every theme's nav color with the system's gray and give up the shell color that keeps a new window from flashing.
notes: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.

title: knip finds no unused file, export or dependency in the app, the engine or the desktop app
when: Runs knip in `app/`, `lathe/` and `desktop/`, each with its own `knip.json`.
then: Expects it to report nothing.

title: An open spec page reloads the data when the server reports spec:changed
when: Opens a record page, changes the served workspace, sends `spec:changed`.
then: Checks that the page fetches the workspace again and shows the new title at the same address.

title: Every class selector in the app stylesheets is used in app/src
when: Reads every stylesheet in `app/src`.
then: Expects each class in a selector to be named in `app/src` or `app/index.html`, or built by a class-building template literal (such as `stage-${stage}`) whose suffix the source names; each failure names the selector, its file and its line.

title: Every command in the keymap is handled and can be reached, and every command a control names is in the keymap
when: Reads `app/src`.
then: Expects every keymap command that is not local to a component or left to the browser to be registered with `useCommand` (so the command palette lists it), every local or browser command to have keys, and every command a button, tooltip or run names to be in the keymap.

title: Every icon in icons.tsx is drawn somewhere
then: Expects each icon in `icons.tsx` to be named by an `Icon` or a control, an icon map, or a view the page bar draws.

title: Every box look, badge and line style the Graph view can draw is in its key
when: Renders the Graph view's legend.
then: Expects an entry, with words beside it, for each look the canvas draws a box in (each stage's colors, a group's, a file's, a domain event's and an open question's), the focus's ring, each shape, a Nested box and a Voronoi cell, the bar, each badge, each line style a relation can take, and the cross-link.

title: Every box, badge and line an ERD draws is in the Model view key
when: Draws the ERD of every domain, aggregate and entity of a workspace with entities and domain events, renders its key.
then: Expects an entry, with words beside it, for each line's relation (dashed where the line is), each box's color, the event flag, the root badge, the highlight and the faded ring; and expects every class the stylesheet gives an ERD box or line to be one the test checks or one that only answers the pointer.

title: In the Tree, Nested and Voronoi layouts, at every domain, stage and folder of every product, at depths 1 to 3 in two panes, siblings share one size and text scale and every drawn box shows its name
when: Loads the repo's own specs (Lathe and the Tool Library), and for each layout and product frames every domain, stage and folder group at depths 1, 2 and 3 in a 770 by 640 and a 1200 by 800 pane with the real camera.
then: Expects the siblings in each map to be the same size (Voronoi cells within 10% of each other's area) with one text scale, every drawn box's label lines to give back its title and its kind and ID line, and the label to fit its box at its scale (a Voronoi cell's inside its outline). On a failure it names the layout, focus, depth, pane, box and its size on screen.

title: Stability: in each layout, focusing each of Lathe's domains at depth 2, framed and zoomed in, every drawn box shows its title text and its whole label inside it
when: In the Tree layout at depth 2 and in the Nested and Voronoi layouts, focuses each of Lathe's five domains, framed and then zoomed in twice.
then: Expects every drawn box in the canvas to show its title text and its whole label inside it, each line as drawn no wider than its place and inside its box, read from the canvas's drawn scene.

title: Performance: zoom and pan on Lathe's map are measured frame by frame in each layout
then: On Lathe's product in the Tree, Nested and Voronoi layouts, zooms the canvas in and out with the wheel about the pointer (twenty steps each way) and pans it with a drag, and prints for each the longest frame, the main-thread work and how many frames took over 20 ms. It is measured, not held to a budget: the re-center budgets (`LA-PLT-T93`) hold the graph's motion.

title: A refused command leaves the data and the files as they were
key: is all or nothing: a refused command leaves the data and the files as they were
when: Applies three commands as one write (add a view, link it, add an automated test with no file), the last of which the store refuses.
then: Expects one problem with rule `check` on command 2, no trace of the view in the records or the database, and every data file unchanged.

title: A write checks the validation queries before any file changes
key: refuses an aggregate with two roots
when: Sets a child entity's role to root, so its aggregate has two roots.
then: Expects the write refused by the `aggregate-root` validation query, naming the aggregate.

title: Every gap between open panes moves by keys, is remembered and resets evenly, and a pane goes full screen until Escape
when: Moves the gap between the wiki and the graph with the arrow and End keys.
then: Expects each pane's weight in the grid with its least width and the weight remembered, double-clicks and expects an even share, puts the graph pane full screen, expects focus on its button, presses Escape and expects the panes back with focus on the full screen button.

title: A link its relation does not allow is refused, though the link table would take it
key: refuses a link its supertype ends allow but its relation does not
when: Links two records whose kinds both fit the link table's supertype ends, but not the relation's pairs.
then: Expects the `relation-pair` validation query to refuse it.

title: A link to another product is refused
key: refuses a link to another product
when: Links a record of one product to a record of another.
then: Expects the `link-crosses-product` validation query to refuse it.

title: A product kind and its records can be declared and added in one write
key: declares a product kind and adds its records in one write
