when: Applies a product kind, its field and a record of it as one write; then a bad date, a kind with a table Lathe has, and a link the product relation does not allow.
then: Expects the new table and its file, the record kept on reopening, and each later write refused with its rule.

title: An add rewrites only its own table's file, sorted, with the ID registered
key: adds a record, registers its ID and rewrites only its table file
when: Adds a requirement.
then: Expects its ID in the registry, only `requirement.jsonl` changed, and the new row on its sorted line with its columns in the table's order.

title: Links and unlinks keep the file sorted by its key columns
key: links and unlinks, keeping the file sorted by its key columns
when: Links and unlinks two records.
then: Expects the relation's file sorted by its key columns after each write.

title: Writes run one after another, each on the state the one before left
key: runs writes one after another, each on the state the one before left
when: Starts three adds at once.
then: Expects all three rows, in order, and a side connection that reads all of them.

title: A refused add names its rule and command: a key that exists, a bad parent, a link table
key: refuses a row whose key exists, a bad parent, and a link table
when: Adds a view with an ID in use, a view under a domain that does not exist, and a row straight into a link table.
then: Expects `primary-key` on command 0, `foreign-key` with the message naming the missing domain, and a `command` refusal that says to use link.

title: A refused set names its rule: a key, a parent, an unknown column or a bad value
key: refuses a key column, a parent column, an unknown column and a bad value
when: Sets a key column, a parent column, a column the table lacks and a value of the wrong type.
then: Expects each refused with its rule and nothing changed.

title: A set changes and clears columns
key: changes and clears columns
when: Sets a column and clears another with null.
then: Expects the row changed and the cleared column left out of its line.

title: A move sets and clears the parent columns, between parents of different kinds
key: moves a record between parents of different kinds, setting and clearing its parent columns
when: Moves a record from one parent kind to another.
then: Expects the new parent's column set, the old one cleared, and the derived columns filled from the new parent.

title: Every command has a title, and no binding clashes or takes a browser key
then: Checks every row of the keymap for an id, title and group, finds no duplicate binding on either platform and no reserved key, shows that the duplicate check catches a clash and a sequence prefix, and checks the VS Code defaults.

title: A move carries what sits inside along to another domain
key: carries what sits inside along to another domain
when: Moves a capability to another domain.
then: Expects its use cases, flows and tests to keep their parent and take the new domain.

title: A move under a parent its kind cannot take, or inside itself, is refused
key: refuses a parent its kind cannot sit under, and a move inside itself
when: Moves a record under a kind it cannot sit under, and a layer under its own sub-layer.
then: Expects both refused with their reasons.

title: A record others reference cannot be removed, and the refusal says what references it
key: refuses a record others reference, saying what references it
when: Removes a record that has children and links to it.
then: Expects the removal refused, naming each referrer.

title: A removal takes the record's parts and the links it starts
key: removes a record with its parts and the links it starts
when: Removes a record with part rows and links of its own.
then: Expects the record, its parts and its links gone from the tables and the files.

title: Two branches that each added a row merge through git with the driver set up as the README says
key: merges two branches that each added a row, through git with the driver set up as the README says
when: Sets up a git repo with `merge.lathe-data.*` and `.gitattributes` as the README says, adds a different row to one data file on two branches, and merges them.
then: Expects the merge to go through with both rows, sorted.

title: Writes through the store and answers with the rows it changed
key: writes through the store and answers with the rows it changed
when: Posts a write the store accepts to the dev API plugin over a copy of a product.
then: Expects 200 with the rows the write changed, and the data file changed on disk.

title: Answers a refused write with every reason and changes nothing
key: answers a refused write with every reason and changes nothing
when: Posts a write the store refuses.
then: Expects 422 with every problem and its command index, and no data file changed.

title: Refuses a write from another site, one not sent as JSON, and one that is not a list of commands
key: refuses a write from another site, one not sent as JSON, and one that is not a list of commands
when: Posts writes from another origin, with another content type and with a body that is not a list of commands.
then: Expects each refused before the store sees it, and no data file changed.

title: Serves the typed data from the data folder, with the schema, and the folder it reads
key: serves the typed data from the data folder, with the schema, and the folder it reads
when: Asks the dev API plugin for GET /api/spec over a product.
then: Expects 200, not cached, with the schema description, the data folder and every stored table's rows.

title: Answers 500 with the reason when the engine cannot be loaded
key: answers 500 with the reason when the engine cannot be loaded
when: Asks for GET /api/spec with an engine that fails to load.
then: Expects 500 with the reason, and no other data.

title: Mod is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere
when: Normalizes and shows bindings for both platforms, turns key events into chords (physical keys with modifiers, characters without), and matches chords and sequences.

title: Reads the data again when a file changes under it
key: reads the data again when a file changes under it
when: Changes a data file behind the dev API plugin, then asks for GET /api/spec.
then: Expects the answer to hold the changed row.

title: Single-key shortcuts never fire while typing
then: Expects inputs, text areas and editable text to count as typing and checkboxes and buttons not to, and single keys to be told apart from chords, function keys and Escape.

title: Bindings can be overridden in local storage, never onto a browser key
when: Stores overrides.
then: Expects unknown commands and local keys ignored, a browser essential dropped, the new binding matched, and bad JSON ignored.

title: Ctrl+P and Ctrl+K open quick find without printing
when: Presses Ctrl+P.
then: Expects the event prevented and quick find focused; collapses the nav and expects Ctrl+K to open it; expects an unhandled Ctrl key left alone.

title: Ctrl+B and Ctrl+Alt+B hide and show the nav and the side bar, announced
when: Presses each twice.
then: Expects the rail, the side bar hidden and shown, and the announcements.

title: Alt+W, Alt+G and Alt+M or Ctrl+1, 2 and 4 toggle the views, and Ctrl+3 shows the focused pane alone
when: Off a Mac, opens and closes views with Ctrl+2, Alt+W, Alt+G and Ctrl+1.
then: Expects the last open view to stay open and say so, expects Ctrl+4 and Alt+M to do nothing where Model is not offered, shows the focused pane alone with Ctrl+3 and back with Ctrl+3 or Escape, and expects the old full screen key to do nothing; expects the address and the announcements.

title: F8 and Shift+F8 move through the problems and say each one
when: On the.
then: Checks page, steps forward and back through the problems, wrapping around, and expects each one announced.

title: The shortcuts sheet and the command palette are searchable, and the palette runs commands
when: Opens the sheet with ?
then: Expects its groups, a shortcut, the override note and the search; expects ? typed into a search box; opens the palette, filters to Graph view on or off, runs it, and finds Expand all and Collapse all.

title: g then c, f or h jumps, with a hint, and not while typing
when: Presses g then c, f and h.
then: Expects Checks, the format and home, the hint while waiting, and nothing while typing in quick find.

title: In the graph, + and - change the depth, t switches trace mode and . frames the focus again
when: Presses + and -.
then: Expects the depth to change, presses . on a domain's graph and expects it still the center, finds no command to open or fold a group in place, and presses t on a requirement's graph and expects trace mode and its files.

title: F12, Shift+F12, Ctrl+Shift+E, Ctrl+Shift+I, / and Ctrl+- move focus and history
when: Opens a focused link with F12, shows incoming links with Shift+F12, focuses the nav and the side bar, focuses quick find or the page search with /, and goes back with Ctrl+-.

title: A tooltip shows a control's name and keys on hover and keyboard focus
then: Expects no tooltip at once on hover, the tooltip after the delay, one at once on keyboard focus, Escape and leaving closing it, and none on a click.

title: Keys are shown as the platform shows them
when: Formats bindings for a Mac and elsewhere, then on a Mac.
then: Expects ⌘B, ⌥⌘B and ⌥1 in tooltips, ⌘P in quick find and ⌘\ in the palette.

title: The palette shows each command's keys right-aligned in kbd styling
then: Expects each palette row to end in a right-aligned `<kbd>` with `aria-keyshortcuts`, and a command without keys to show none.

title: A rebinding changes every hint
when: Overrides two bindings.
then: Expects the tooltips, `aria-keyshortcuts`, the palette and the sheet to show the new keys.

title: Every control with a shortcut has aria-keyshortcuts
then: Expects `aria-keyshortcuts` on the nav toggle, quick find, the spaces, Checks, the view toggles (Alt+W and Alt+G first, off a Mac) and the side bar toggles, the depth buttons and full screen (Ctrl+3), and none for a sequence.

title: The shortcuts sheet matches the hints
then: Expects one Switch to row per product with the keys its tooltip shows.

title: Layout lives in the markup: no stylesheet rule moves or restyles an element from outside its component
when: Reads `app/src/styles.css`.
then: Expects no `display: contents` and no `:has()`. Then opens a record page and expects its Children section's Expand all inside the section's own header row.

title: Styles are set by class: no selector names only elements, beyond the base styles
when: Reads every style rule in `app/src/styles.css` (not keyframe steps).
then: Expects each selector to name a class, attribute or ID, unless it names only base elements.

title: Colors and shadows are tokens: color values appear only where :root defines them
then: Expects no hex, `rgb()` or `hsl()` value in any style rule outside `:root`, and no color in a component's inline style.

title: Generic components know nothing of specs, the graph or the shell: they import only React and each other
when: Reads every file in `app/src/components`.
then: Expects imports only from React, React DOM and the same folder.

title: Kind labels become plural only through plural() and lowercase only through lowerLabel()
when: Reads the app's source, apart from `plural.ts`.
then: Expects no template or sum that adds an "s" to a label. It also expects no label lowercased by hand with `toLowerCase()`.

title: Every button and link on the main pages has an accessible name
when: Opens the product list, a domain page, a record page and a record's graph.
then: Expects every visible button, link and form control to have an accessible name.

title: Code, specs and docs use American spelling
when: Reads the app and engine source, every data file and the READMEs.
then: Expects none of a list of British spellings (`aria-labelledby` excepted).

title: Everything clickable shows a hover state: each pointer-cursor rule has a :hover rule for the same class
when: Reads every style rule in `app/src/styles.css` that sets a pointer cursor.
then: Expects a `:hover` rule naming the same class, and expects the shared hover tokens to be defined.

title: The workbench: panels sit on the shell a gap apart, and every gap between two panels is the one ResizeHandle
then: Expects the shell, gap and radius tokens, no separator drawn outside ResizeHandle, and on a record with the wiki and graph open the navigation, the gap between the panes and the side bar as resize handles beside panels.

title: Every grid says its columns, a single column being minmax(0, 1fr), so content shrinks with its panel
when: Reads every style rule.
then: Expects each grid, other than a centering icon grid, to declare its columns.

title: A handle resizes its panel with the arrow keys, Shift, Home and End, remembers it, and double-click resets it
when: Steps the navigation's gap with Right, Shift and Left, and End.
then: Expects the stored and applied width, resets it by double-click, and steps the side bar's gap, where Left grows it, and Home.

title: Remembered sizes come back, out-of-range ones fall back to the default, and the narrow layout has no handles
when: Starts with a remembered navigation width and an out-of-range side bar width.
then: Expects the first kept and the second back to its default; on a narrow screen expects no resize handles.

title: The page bar holds the page's tabs and layout controls; each pane's header holds only that pane's actions, on wide and narrow screens
when: Opens a record alone, with the wiki and graph, and with both on a phone.
then: Expects one page bar, outside every pane and the side bar, holding the tab strip at its left (on a phone, the Open pages button instead), and at its right the one "View" group of `aria-pressed` toggles, one pressed per shown pane, with the side bar toggle last. On a wide screen each pane is a panel whose first child is its slim header: a non-interactive label naming its view, and only its close button (when more than one pane is open) and its full screen button, all icon buttons, with no tabs or groups in it. On a phone one pane shows, with no header. The title sits in the leftmost pane, and the stylesheet gives the page bar and the pane headers fixed heights.

title: Motion is shared and optional: every transition and animation uses the motion or hover tokens and is turned off under reduced motion
when: Reads every style rule in `app/src/styles.css` that sets a transition or animation.
then: Expects its times and easing to come from `--motion-speed`, `--motion-ease` or `--hover-speed`, and each such selector to be turned off by a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule or to apply only under `no-preference`. Expects the tokens to be defined, and code that animates frame by frame to take its timing from `readMotion()`, which reads them and checks `prefers-reduced-motion`.

title: The page bar holds the tabs, then the view toggles, a divider and the side bar toggle; each pane header names its view and holds its close and full screen buttons, with one on look
when: Opens a record in the Wiki view.
then: Expects the page bar to hold the active tab for the record at its left and, in order, the Wiki and Graph toggles (no Model on a use case), the divider and the side bar toggle, with the pressed view and the shown side bar both `icon-button is-on`, and the wiki pane's header to name its view and hold only Full screen. Opens the graph and expects each pane's header to hold its close and full screen buttons, the page bar unchanged, no tab strip in a pane, focus kept on the Graph toggle, and the title in the leftmost pane.

title: Reloading brings back the same tabs, the preview, the active tab and each tab's views
when: Opens three tabs, two kept and one preview, with different views, activates the first, and reloads the app at the same address.
then: Expects the same tabs in order, the same preview and active tab, the first tab's two panes, and the second tab's wiki alone when activated.

title: Clicking a box goes to it, boxes show a hover state, and a key under the diagram explains the colors with emoji squares and the line ends
when: Opens a domain with the wiki and model.
then: Expects the key under the diagram with 🟦 and ⬜ and the line ends, clicks an aggregate's box and expects its page with the same views, presses Enter on an entity's box and expects its page, and expects the hover ring, its speed and the colors as tokens in the stylesheet.

title: With three panes open each gap is its own handle, resizing only the two panes beside it
when: Opens the wiki, graph and model on an aggregate, steps the gap between the graph and the model.
then: Expects only those two panes' weights to change, then double-clicks it and expects them even again.

title: The view toggles have Ctrl+W, Ctrl+G and Ctrl+M on a Mac and Alt+W, Alt+G and Alt+M elsewhere, then Ctrl+1, 2 and 4, and no platform is offered a browser key
when: Resolves the keymap for a Mac and for other platforms.
then: Expects each view toggle's keys, Ctrl+W to match on a Mac but not Cmd+W, Alt+G but not Ctrl+G elsewhere, an override to Ctrl+W or Ctrl+G dropped off a Mac, and no binding reserved on its platform.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link: every record row on the domain and record pages has exactly one row link, stretched over the row
when: Renders a domain page and a record page.
then: Expects every row of every `record-list` (each tree item's own row, and each plain row) that holds a record link to have exactly one `row-link`, a real link to a record's page. Reads `app/src/styles.css` and expects the `row-link` `::after` to be absolute with `inset: 0`, the rows to be `position: relative`, the row's other controls to sit above it with a `z-index`, and the link to give the row a hover tint and a focus ring.

title: Color theme previews each theme as it is arrowed to; Enter keeps it and Escape puts back the one before
when: Opens the picker with g then t, arrows to Workshop.
then: Expects it shown but not kept, Escape to put Lathe back, then filters to Midnight and keeps it with Enter, remembered with its stylesheet and announced.

title: Light, dark or system is a command and a choice on the Appearance page
when: Runs the mode command from the palette, previews and keeps Dark, then follows the nav footer's Appearance link and switches to System and Light there, each applied at once and remembered.

title: The Appearance page lists every theme with a preview, and a copy is edited live, renamed, reset and deleted
then: Expects the five built-ins with previews in their own colors, uses one, duplicates Workshop into an editor with colors grouped by purpose and light and dark side by side, changes a color, text size, radius, density, motion and a font and sees each in the theme's stylesheet at once, renames it, resets it to Workshop and deletes it, after which Lathe is in use again.

title: A color below WCAG AA while editing gets a warning beside its swatch
when: Sets the light muted text to a pale gray.
then: Expects warnings with the ratio on paper and on sheet in the light cell only, and a value that is not a color to be refused.

title: A theme exports as a versioned file and imports back, and anything but known tokens is refused
then: Round-trips a theme file, refuses another version or format, unknown fields, unknown tokens and values that reach past the token, fills a partial file from Lathe, and imports a file on the Appearance page as a theme of one's own.

title: The early script puts the chosen theme and mode on the page before the app runs
when: Runs the inline script from index.html with a stored stylesheet, theme and mode.
then: Expects them on the page, and with nothing stored expects the stylesheet's own Lathe theme following the system.

title: Themes only set tokens: a theme file holds token names only, its stylesheet sets them on :root, and every built-in passes AA
when: Reads every built-in theme file.
then: Expects only token names the stylesheet's `:root` defines; expects each theme's stylesheet to have only `:root` selectors and custom properties; and computes the contrast of ink, muted text and the accent on paper and sheet for every built-in in both modes.

title: The built-in themes: Lathe is the stylesheet unchanged, High contrast reaches AAA, and the others pass AA throughout
when: Compares the Lathe theme file with the stylesheet's `:root` and dark values.
then: Expects High contrast's body and muted text at 7:1 or more in both modes, and every pair the editor checks to pass in each other built-in.

title: A phone shows a compact top bar with the title and a step up, and one view at a time switched from the page bar, leaving the views remembered for a wide screen alone
when: On a phone, opens a record with `?view=wiki,graph`.
then: Expects the top bar's menu, title, link up to the domain (keeping the views) and quick find; the wiki alone with no pane headers or handles; then switches to the graph and expects `?view=graph`, the graph alone, and the remembered views unchanged. A domain's link goes up to its product.

title: The side bar is a bottom sheet: it opens at half height with focus inside, its handle takes it to full height and back, Escape closes it and focus returns
when: On a phone, opens the side bar from the page bar.
then: Expects a modal bottom sheet at half height with the side bar focused, full height and back from the handle, Tab kept inside, and Escape closing it with focus back on the toggle.

title: A drag on a sheet's handle settles by distance and speed
then: Checks `settle`: up to full height, a short drag staying put, a flick up, down to half from full, away from half by a long drag or a flick, and away from full by a very long drag.

title: The open pages are a sheet from the page bar
when: On a phone, opens the Open pages sheet, keeps the preview tab from its row, opens another page.
then: Expects two rows with the active one marked and focused; choosing a row goes there and closes the sheet; a row's close button closes its tab.

title: Quick find on a phone is a full-screen sheet
when: On a phone, opens quick find from the top bar.
then: Expects a dialog with the box focused, the results inline under it, a choice going to the record and closing the sheet, and Escape closing it with focus back on the button.

title: The nav is a full-screen sheet that keeps Tab inside it
when: On a phone, opens the nav.
then: Expects the sheet, Tab from its last control going to its first and Shift+Tab from its first to its last.

title: The theme-color meta follows the theme's --sheet token
when: Sets `--sheet` on the root.
then: Expects the meta to take it, changes it and expects the meta to follow.

title: Everything works by touch: on a coarse pointer every clickable control is at least 44 × 44 px
when: Reads `app/src/styles.css`.
then: Expects every rule with a pointer cursor to be covered by a coarse-pointer rule that sizes the control (or a `::before` stretched around it) to `--touch-target` (44 px), or to be touch-sized everywhere; canvas nodes and cards are exempt, being laid out large and zoomable.

title: Nothing is reachable only by hover
when: Reads the stylesheet.
then: Expects every control a hover reveals to be shown always on a coarse pointer, and the tooltip to open on keyboard focus as well as hover.

title: No page scrolls sideways at 320 px
when: Reads the stylesheet for any fixed least width over 288 px outside a wide-screen query.
then: Checks that tables and code blocks scroll in their own box and that IDs wrap, and renders the product, domain, record, component, checks and format pages on a phone expecting every table and code block in a scrolling box and no inline width over 288 px. jsdom lays nothing out, so the real widths are checked in a browser at 320 and 375 px.

title: Stability: the first load of the product, domain and record pages shifts nothing, also with slow fonts
when: Loads each page with the probes installed before its scripts, and once with the app's font files held back 2.5 seconds.
then: Expects no unexpected shift and the nav, the page, the first pane's bar and title and the side bar never to move.

title: Stability: moving between records through the nav, a link, a graph click, Back and quick find keeps the frame still
when: Moves between records each way.
then: Expects the frame not to move; from a page scrolled half-way, expects the new page never to be drawn at the old scroll, and Back to draw the page once, with the row that was at the top of the view back in its place.

title: Stability: opening, closing and maximizing panes and the side bar moves only the panes
when: Opens and closes the Graph and Model panes (Ctrl+2, Ctrl+4, Ctrl+1), full screen (Ctrl+3, Escape) and the side bar.
then: Expects the nav and side bar to stay, open panes not to be drawn anew, and a canvas to appear already fitted.

title: Stability: folding a row and Expand all move only what is below
when: Opens and closes a row and uses Expand all and Collapse all on the domain page.
then: Expects the row, the section heading, the title and the frame to stay.

title: Stability: dragging each gap follows the pointer, and folding by drag moves nothing on the far side
when: Drags the nav, pane and side bar gaps and folds the nav and the side bar by drag.
then: Expects the boxes beside each gap never to jump back and the far side not to move.

title: Stability: re-centering the graph at depth 1 to 3, changing depth and moving around the ERD keep the canvas still
when: Re-centers twice at each depth, changes the depth, and goes from a domain's ERD to an aggregate's and an entity's and back.
then: Expects the pane title, the graph header, the Model header and key and the canvas never to move or remount; the boxes the camera brings into view are drawn inside the canvas.

title: Stability: a live reload keeps what is in view
when: Changes a data file in the suite's copy of the data while the domain page is scrolled half-way (a paragraph added to the domain's description, above the view) and while the graph is open (a paragraph added to the record's goal).
then: Expects what was at the top of the view to stay there, the scroll box to keep its place, and the frame and the graph not to be drawn anew.

title: Stability: tooltips, quick find, the palette and the shortcuts sheet are placed before they show
when: Hovers a toolbar button, types in quick find, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet.
then: Expects each to stay where it showed and the page behind not to move.

title: Nothing jumps, in the source: scroll boxes keep their gutter, bars have one height, counts are one text, canvases stay mounted
when: Reads `app/src/styles.css`.
then: Expects every vertical scroll box to set `scrollbar-gutter: stable` or hide its scrollbar, and the pane title above a canvas, the graph's trail and toolbar, and the Model view's caption and key to have a fixed block size or be one line. Renders the graph and expects its count to be one text after the depth, and its canvas to stay mounted when it re-centers. Reads the graph and Model view sources and expects what the graph connects to reach the host in a layout effect, and the ERD to be fitted before paint and to observe its size once. Moves to a record from outside the nav and expects the nav's domain row to stay closed and be marked, and opening it to open the branch down to the page. Reads `app/index.html` and `app/src/fonts.css` and expects no Google Fonts, the six latin files preloaded, every face `font-display: optional`, and each family's license beside its files.

title: Stability: switching theme moves nothing
when: Switches from the default theme to Midnight through the Color theme pick (g t) on a record page with the graph open.
then: Expects no layout shift at all and no key element to move.

title: Stability: the mobile sheets at 375 px move nothing behind them
when: At 375 px wide with touch, opens and closes the nav drawer, the quick find sheet and the side bar sheet.
then: Expects the top bar, the page and its title behind them not to move.

title: Actions look like actions on the main pages
when: Renders the products, product, domain, record, graph.
then: Checks, format and appearance pages and expects no `button.secondary` or `.tree-bulk`, no paragraph whose only content is a plain link (a standalone link must be drawn as a button; a record's own ID line is a reference), and every `<button>` to be the `Button` component's or one of the allowed controls: tab close buttons, toggles in a group, fold chevrons, the nav's rows and rail, the sheet handle, the open-pages list, the title bar's command center and the canvas library's zoom controls. Then reads the source for the same: no `secondary` or `tree-bulk` class, and every raw `<button>` outside `Button.tsx` one of those controls, none taking the Button's own classes except the view toggles, which take the icon look on a wide screen and a segment's on a phone.

title: The Button component draws ghost, primary and icon buttons, and links as buttons
when: Renders `Button` in each variant.
then: Expects a `<button type="button">` with the ghost classes by default, the primary classes when asked, the `icon-button` class and an accessible name for the icon variant, a leading icon when given one, and a real `<a href>` with the button's classes when given `href`. Reads the stylesheet for the ghost hover tint, the primary fill and the coarse-pointer target.

title: One address per thing: only address.ts makes a record or group address, and every address is an ID or a lowercase app page
when: Reads every source file in `app/src` and `desktop/src` except `address.ts`.
then: Expects no path built by hand under `/records`, `/specs` or `/graph`, nor a template starting `/${…}`. Expects every app page's first word to be lowercase and never an ID, `/` to be the products, an ID to be a product, domain or record page and an ID with a kind a group. Then renders the products, a product, a domain, a record, a group, Checks, the format and Appearance, and expects every in-app link to be `/`, an app page or an ID.

title: A domain's ERD draws one dashed reacts-to line per aggregate pair and event, from the aggregate raising it to the one reacting, with the event's name as its label on hover
when: Builds a domain's ERD.
then: Expects exactly one dashed line per aggregate's `reacts_to` link to another aggregate's event, both ways across a domain boundary, none for an aggregate's own event, the other domain's lines as context, and reacts-to lines fanned wider apart. Renders it and expects each line's hover label to be its event's name over a wider stroke, shown on the shared hover speed (none under reduced motion) and always by touch.

title: An aggregate's page lists its domain events titled "Domain events", each row a whole link saying what raises it and how many react; an event's page shows its Fields table, "Raised by" and "Reacted to by", and a reacting record shows "Reacts to"
when: Opens an aggregate's page.
then: Expects its Domain events list, one link per row with "Raised by" and "Reacted to by" counts, and the events left out of its Entities list; follows a row to the event and expects its Fields table and its Traceability's "Raised by" and "Reacted to by" groups with no relation codes; opens a reacting aggregate and expects "Reacts to".

title: The side bar's switcher, its headings, and its state per view mode and per tab across a reload
then: Expects the side bar closed in the Wiki view and open on Details in the Graph view, a "Side bar views" group of three pressed-or-not buttons, each view under its heading, focus kept on the button pressed, Outline still chosen in the Graph view after a reload, and the Wiki view of the same tab still closed.

title: Outline lists the wiki's sections, scrolls to one and marks it, and lists the Model view's boxes
then: Expects the wiki's Traceability and Problems sections among the outline's rows, a click to scroll the wiki pane and mark that row `aria-current="location"`, and a domain's Model view outline to list its aggregates as whole-row links.

title: Stability: switching the side bar's view and hovering graph nodes moves nothing outside the side bar
when: On a record with the wiki and the graph open, switches the side bar to Outline, History and Details, then hovers three nodes and leaves.
then: Expects no unexpected layout shift and the nav, the pane bars and titles, the graph's header and canvas, the side bar and its switcher to keep their boxes.

title: Performance: the first load ships 250 KB of JavaScript or less
when: Builds the app for production.
then: Expects the JavaScript that `index.html` loads at once (its scripts and module preloads) to be 250 KB or less gzipped; prints the largest chunks.

title: Performance: a record page is interactive within 1.5 s
when: Opens a record page three times on a warm server.
then: Expects the median time from navigation until its title is drawn and the long frames after it have ended to be under 1.5 s.

title: Performance: a view switch takes under 100 ms of main-thread work
when: On a record page, opens and closes the Graph pane (after a first open has loaded its code).
then: Expects each switch to take under 100 ms of main-thread work.

title: Performance: a graph re-center at depth 3 takes under 500 ms of main-thread work and glides at 60 Hz
when: In the Tree layout at depth 3 and in the Nested layout (which has no depth), re-centers three times on boxes in view.
then: Expects each re-center, from the click until the glide has ended, to take under 500 ms of main-thread work, at most 3 of its frames to take more than 20 ms and none 100 ms or more; prints each re-center's work, its longest frame and how many frames took over 20 ms.

title: Performance: opening the Model pane takes under 100 ms of main-thread work
when: On an aggregate, opens the Model pane once (loading its code and ELK, measured without a budget), closes it, opens it again.
then: Expects that switch to take under 100 ms of main-thread work; measures how long a domain's ERD takes to be drawn after its page.

title: Performance: memory after 50 navigations
then: With the wiki and the graph open, moves through 50 records and measures the JavaScript heap after a garbage collection, before and after, without a budget, so a leak shows in the report.

title: The first load reaches no React Flow and no ELK through static imports
when: Walks the static imports from `app/src/main.tsx` through the app's own modules.
then: Expects none to import `@xyflow/react` (its stylesheet aside) or `elkjs`, naming the file, line and import path of any that does, so the first-load budget is guarded without a browser.

title: Accessibility: every page and state passes axe at WCAG 2.2 AA, at both widths, in every look
when: Opens each page and state (the product, domain, record and group pages, the graph, the Model view.
then: Checks, Format, Appearance, quick find, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, a tooltip, the nav drawer, the quick find sheet and the side bar sheet) at 1440 px and 375 px, in Lathe and High contrast, light and dark, and expects axe-core to find nothing.

title: Accessibility: Tab reaches every control and comes back round, with no trap
when: On a record page with the wiki and the graph open, presses Tab until focus comes back to its first stop.
then: Expects it to get there, every stop to be drawn, and Shift+Tab to go back the same way.

title: Accessibility: the main tasks by keyboard alone, with their announcements
when: With the keyboard only: follows the skip link, opens a record from the nav and from quick find, turns the Graph view on and off from the page bar, moves between the graph's boxes and re-centers on one, folds and unfolds a row, hides, shows and focuses the side bar, and picks the Midnight theme.
then: Expects the announcer to say "Graph view", "Side bar hidden", "Side bar shown" and "Color theme: Midnight".

title: Coverage counts satisfied and proved requirements and lists the gaps
when: Loads a fixture with known `satisfies` and `proves` links.
then: Expects the domain's coverage counts and gaps to match.

title: Coverage counts designed, built and proved separately
when: Loads a fixture where one requirement is satisfied by a component whose file exists, one by a component whose file is missing, and one by nothing.
then: Expects designed 2, built 1 and proved 1, with built never above designed in any fixture.

title: Coverage gaps are warnings, so an unfinished design has no errors
when: Loads the unfinished fixture.
then: Expects `unsatisfied`, `unproved` and `component-file-missing` warnings and no errors.

title: Coverage counts every obligation kind in meta-model order, including interaction requirements
when: Loads a fixture with domain rules, requirements and interaction requirements.
then: Expects one entry per obligation kind, in schema order, with the right counts.

title: Only automated and manual tests prove; a planned test makes an obligation planned
when: Loads a fixture with a test with no state, a manual test and a planned test.
then: Expects only the first two to prove, the planned one to count as planned, and the `unproved` warning to say so.

title: An extension's obligation kind and design and proof relations are counted like the defaults
when: Loads a fixture whose product declares an obligation kind and design and proof relations, one of them from a kind that is not a component.
then: Expects them counted, with the design from the other kind counting as designed but not built.

title: The meta-model's obligation and role columns are loaded into the workspace
when: Loads a fixture with Lathe's kinds and relations only, one with a product's own obligation kind and design relation, and one with a product kind that is not an obligation and a relation with no role.
then: Expects Lathe's obligation kinds and design and proof relations in the workspace, the product's obligation kind and design relation read the same way, and the others with no obligation and no role.

title: The check prints one coverage line per domain and obligation kind, with planned counts
when: Runs `lathe check` on a fixture.
then: Expects one coverage line per domain and obligation kind with designed, built, proved and planned counts.

title: A rule test keyed by the rule's ID needs no test ID in code
when: Loads a test record whose `file` names only the domain rule it proves, never the test's own ID.
then: Expects no error on it.

title: A test file that names neither the test nor a record it proves is an error
when: Loads an automated test that proves one rule while its file names another.
then: Expects a `proof-not-in-file` error naming the file, the test and the rule it proves.

title: A rule can be not applicable in one domain and owed in another
then: Expects a rule naming a setting to be not applicable where every following use case marks it so, with the reasons, and owed where one gives a value.

title: The domain page lists the patterns it follows
when: Opens a domain page.
then: Expects its followed pattern with the following use case, the rules folded under it, and per rule its designed, built, proved and planned marks.

title: Not applicable shows its use case and reason
then: Expects a not applicable rule to show the use case as a link and its reason, beside a rule the domain proves.

title: Coverage shows the pattern rule line
then: Expects the domain's coverage to show the pattern rule line with its counts, and gaps naming the rule.

title: A domain that follows no pattern says so
when: Opens a domain with no following use case.
then: Expects the section to say so.

title: A pattern page shows its settings, rules and followers
when: Opens a pattern page.
then: Expects the settings table with dependent rules, the rules once, and each following domain with its use cases and their setting values.

title: A pattern page shows each domain's status per rule
then: Expects each following domain's table to give each rule's status in that domain.

title: A pattern rule page lists the domains that owe it
when: Opens a pattern rule page.
then: Expects both following domains; then a pattern nobody follows, which says so.

title: The planned bar says how many more obligations, already proved, still have a planned test
then: Expects `1 more planned`, with its hover text, on a domain rule's planned bar where `planned_any` is 1 and `planned` 0, on the product and domain pages, and nothing where the two are equal.

title: Each domain's coverage shows its tests by state, on the product and domain pages
then: Expects `Tests 1 automated, 1 manual, 1 planned` on a domain card and on the domain page, with the planned count explained as not proof.

title: A test file names an ID only as a whole ID
when: Loads a test that proves `PX-D-DR03` while its file names only `PX-D-DR030` and `PX-D-DR03-R01`.
then: Expects a `proof-not-in-file` error.

title: The summary counts the product's tests by state, and planned beside proof
then: Expects the Summary's Tests row to total its domains and its Planned row to add `; 1 more planned beside proof`, with the proved count unchanged.

title: A pattern the domain itself follows is listed, followed by the whole domain, and every rule applies
when: Makes a domain follow a pattern directly.
then: Expects the pattern among the domain's followed patterns with no use cases, a rule with a setting still applying, and its row on the domain page reading "followed by the whole domain".

title: An obligation lists Designed by, Proved by and Carried out in, each component marked built
when: Opens a requirement's content.
then: Expects its Traceability groups in order (Designed by, Proved by, Carried out in), the designing component marked built, kind tags only in the list that mixes kinds, and no gap callout for a requirement that is designed and proved.

title: Gap callouts agree with coverage, link to their check, and a pattern rule has one line per domain
then: Expects "Not proved yet" and "Not designed yet" callouts linked to the unproved and unsatisfied check pages, a pattern rule judged in each domain owing it (not built and only planned in one, designed, built and proved in the other, and a rule not applicable in a domain left out there), and every coverage gap of every domain matched by a callout.

title: A use case shows a requirement table, then what carries it out, follows and applies
then: Expects a use case's table with the columns Requirement, Designed, Built and Proved, one row per requirement in ID order, cells linking the designing component and the proving test or flagging "not proved", then the groups Carried out by flow and Applies, the applied rule showing its own coverage mark.

title: A component shows Satisfies and Proved through; a test shows Proves and its file with its state
then: Expects a component's groups Satisfies, Proved through (the test proving what it designs) and Implements, and a test's Proves and Run by, the file shown with the test's state and flagged missing with a link to the test-file-missing check.

title: Supports links show as Supported by on the obligation and Supports on the test, never as proof
then: Expects a domain rule that a test supports to list the test under Supported by and not under Proved by, and the test to list the rule under Supports.

title: A domain rule under its domain shows the aggregates it involves under "Involves", and each aggregate shows it under "Involved in"; an interaction requirement's Carries out is not repeated
when: Reads the `involves` relation's labels, and opens a domain rule under its domain that involves two aggregates.
then: Expects its Traceability to list them under Involves, the aggregate's to list the rule under Involved in, and an interaction requirement's Traceability to leave out the Carries out its own section shows.

title: A rule no follower meets is waived in that domain, neither owed nor proved
then: Expects rules that apply when scope is not single, or is many, to be left out of the coverage and warnings of a domain whose only use case gives scope single, a proof of one there to count for nothing, and both to be owed in a domain where one use case gives " Many ".

title: A domain that follows a pattern itself meets an applies-when setting only through the settings it gives
then: Expects a domain that follows the pattern itself and gives scope single, one that gives no settings, and one whose use case gives scope a not-applicable reason, to owe the rules with no condition but not those no follower meets.

title: A test state other than automated, manual or planned is refused
when: Loads a test with the state `someday`, and one with no state.
then: Expects the first refused as a value outside automated, manual and planned, and the second refused as a missing required column.

title: A rule no follower meets shows as Waived here, with the value given, and the gaps leave it out
then: Expects a rule that applies when the record is a basket to apply where a use case gives " Basket " and to read "Waived here: record is Payment" on the domain page and the rule page of a domain that gives Payment, whose Traceability lists only the owing domain; a domain that follows the pattern itself and gives the value meets it.

title: An automated test needs a file; a manual or planned test does not
when: Loads an automated, a manual and a planned test with no `file`.
then: Expects the store to refuse the automated test by its table's check, and to load the manual and planned tests with no error on them.

title: A manual or planned test's file is checked only for existing
when: Loads a manual test naming a missing file, and a planned test naming an existing file that does not mention it.
then: Expects `test-file-missing` on the manual test, no error on the planned one, and no error from any other check.

title: A test state is one lower-case value, read the same way by the checks and by coverage
when: Loads a test whose state is `Manual`, and a manual test that proves a domain rule.
then: Expects the first refused, and the rule the manual test proves counted as proved with no problem on the test.

title: A planned test that names a file not written yet is a warning, not an error
when: Loads a workspace with a planned test whose `file` does not exist.
then: Expects one `test-file-missing` warning and no errors.

title: A use case that gives no value for one of its pattern's settings is an error
then: Expects one `pattern-setting-missing` error, naming the `audit` setting, for a use case that gives a value for `permission` but not for `audit`.

title: A not-applicable setting value counts as given only with a reason: an empty reason is refused
when: Loads a use case that gives one setting a not-applicable reason and nothing for another, and setting values with an empty reason and with neither a value nor a reason.
then: Expects `pattern-setting-missing` for the missing setting only, none in a well-formed fixture, and the store to refuse the empty reason and the value with neither.

title: Two patterns' settings of one name are separate values: a use case gives each pattern its own
when: Loads a use case that follows two patterns which both have an `audit` setting, and gives a value for the first pattern only.
then: Expects one `pattern-setting-missing` error naming the second pattern and `audit`, and the use case's one `audit` value kept for the first pattern alone.

title: A pattern rule is an obligation under a pattern, designed by components and proved by tests
then: Expects the `pattern_rule` kind with parent `pattern` as an obligation, `satisfies` and `proves` rules with design and proof roles, a rule record with no domain and its `setting` field, and no errors in the fixture.

title: Each domain that follows a pattern owes its rules, on one pattern rule line
then: Expects one `pattern_rule` coverage line in a following domain that counts both of the pattern's rules, designed, built and proved, and both rules counted in other following domains.

title: A domain that does not follow the pattern does not owe its rules
then: Expects a total of 0 pattern rules, no pattern rule gaps and no pattern rule warnings for a domain whose use case does not follow the pattern.

title: Only the domain's own components and tests design and prove a pattern rule there
when: A component and a test in one domain cover both rules.
then: Expects other following domains to count no proof from them. Design per domain, asked only when a product makes pattern rules full obligations, is tested by LA-TRC-T58.

title: Built and planned are counted per domain too
then: Expects a domain whose only test of a rule is planned to count it planned, not proved, with designed and built equal to the total since pattern rules need proof only.

title: A rule whose setting every following use case marks not applicable does not apply in that domain
when: Both following use cases in a domain give the rule's setting a not-applicable reason.
then: Expects the rule neither counted nor reported there.

title: A rule still applies when only some following use cases mark its setting not applicable
when: One following use case gives the setting a not-applicable reason and another gives it a value.
then: Expects both rules' `proves` gaps in that domain.

title: A rule that names no setting applies in every following domain
then: Expects the rule with no `setting` counted in every following domain, including the one where the other rule is Not applicable.

title: Gaps name the pattern rule in each domain that lacks it
then: Expects no pattern rule gaps in the domain that proves both rules, and in another the exact `proves` gaps it still has, with no `satisfies` gaps since pattern rules need proof only.

title: An undesigned pattern rule is reported once for each domain that owes it
then: Expects no `unsatisfied` warning for pattern rules by default, since they need proof only; the per-domain warning naming the rule and the domain, when a product asks for design, is tested by LA-TRC-T58.

title: An unproved pattern rule is reported once for each domain that owes it, saying when its test is only planned
then: Expects one `unproved` warning per rule and owing domain with no proving test of its own, and the message for a domain whose only test is planned to say so.

title: A rule naming one of its pattern settings, or none, loads and is not reported
when: Loads a rule naming one of its pattern's settings with an applies-when setting, and a rule with no setting.
then: Expects both to load with no refusal, and no error on the fixture's pattern records.

title: A pattern that no use case follows is a warning
then: Expects a `pattern-not-followed` warning on a pattern with rules (saying how many are not counted) and on one with none, and none in a workspace where every pattern is followed.

title: The rules of a pattern nobody follows count in no domain and are not reported as outside one
then: Expects no gap and no problem on an unfollowed pattern's rules, and no `obligation-outside-domain` warning for pattern rules.

title: Any other obligation outside every domain is a warning
when: Loads a domain rule without a domain, and a product's own obligation kind declared under the product.
then: Expects the rule refused as a missing required column, and exactly one `obligation-outside-domain` warning, on the product's record.

title: TL-LEND designs and proves every Librarian action rule
when: Loads this repository.
then: Expects the Tool Library's Lending domain to owe all three Librarian action rules, each designed, built and proved there, with no pattern left unfollowed.

title: A file that names the test's own ID accepts all its claims
when: Loads a test that proves two rules while its file names only the test's ID.
then: Expects no error on it.

title: A file that names every ID the test proves needs no test ID
when: Loads a test that proves two rules while its file names both rules and not the test.
then: Expects no error on it.

title: A file that names only some of the IDs the test proves is an error for each one left out
when: Loads a test that proves two rules while its file names one.
then: Expects one `proof-not-in-file` error, for the other.

title: A file that names none of the IDs gives one error per proved ID, naming the test, the ID and the file
when: Loads a test that proves three rules while its file names none of them nor the test.
then: Expects three `proof-not-in-file` errors whose messages name the test, the rule and the file, and no `test-file-missing-id`.

title: A test with a key is accepted when its file contains the key, though it names no ID
when: Loads a test with a `key` whose file contains the key and names no ID.
then: Expects no error on it.

title: A test with a key whose file lacks the key is an error, even if the file names the test's ID
when: Loads a test with a `key` whose file names the test and its rule but not the key.
then: Expects exactly one `test-file-missing-id` error quoting the key.

title: A proved ID is found in the file only as a whole ID
when: Loads a test that proves `CL-D-DR04` while its file names only `CL-D-DR040` and `CL-D-DR04-R01`.
then: Expects a `proof-not-in-file` error for `CL-D-DR04`.

title: A test that proves nothing and whose file lacks its ID is a test-file-missing-id error
when: Loads a test with no `proves` links whose file does not name it.
then: Expects one `test-file-missing-id` error.

title: A manual or planned test's file is not checked for its claims
when: Loads a manual and a planned test that each prove two rules while their file names one.
then: Expects no error on either.

title: An automated test whose file backs neither its ID nor its claim leaves the obligation unproved, as coverage does
when: Proves three rules with three automated tests: one whose file names nothing, one whose file names its rule, and one whose file names its own ID.
then: Expects `unproved` and a coverage gap for the first rule only, with its `proof-not-in-file` error.

title: planned_any counts every obligation a planned test is meant to prove, proved or not
when: Loads `owed-proof`, where requirements are proved by automated and manual tests with planned tests beside them, one has only planned tests and one only automated tests.
then: Expects `planned_any` 3 of 4 beside `planned` 1.

title: A pattern rule has proof owed only in a domain whose own planned test is meant to prove it
then: Expects the pattern rule's `planned_any` to be 1 in the domain with a planned test for it and 0 in the other following domain, where only an automated test proves it.

title: Each domain counts its own tests by state, which every test gives
then: Expects 2 automated, 1 manual and 2 planned in one domain, 1 automated in another, zero in a domain with no tests and every test counted once, and the store to refuse a test with no state or with `Planned`.

title: planned_any is never less than planned nor more than the total, in every fixture
when: Loads several fixtures.
then: Checks, for every domain and obligation kind, that `planned <= planned_any <= total`, and that every domain reports its tests by the three states.

title: lathe check shows proof owed where it differs from planned, and each domain's tests by state
when: Runs `lathe check` on `owed-proof`.
then: Expects `; 3/4 with a planned test` on the line where it differs, nothing added where it is equal, and one tests line per domain.

title: A domain that follows a pattern itself owes every one of its rules, even where its use cases say not applicable
when: A domain follows a pattern itself while its one use case gives a rule's setting a not-applicable reason.
then: Expects that rule still owed there, with its `proves` gap and `unproved` warning naming the domain.

title: A domain follows a pattern when it or any of its use cases follows it, and owes each rule once
when: A domain follows one pattern itself and another through its use case.
then: Expects one Pattern rule line counting the rules of both, each once.

title: Not applicable still works through use-case setting values when the domain follows only through its use cases
when: Every following use case of a domain gives a rule's setting a not-applicable reason.
then: Expects that rule not counted and nothing reported for it there.

title: A domain that follows no pattern, itself or through a use case, owes no pattern rule
then: Expects a total of 0 and no gaps on the Pattern rule line of a domain that follows nothing.

title: A pattern may have no settings; its rules apply wherever it is followed and nothing asks for settings
when: A pattern with no `pattern_setting` rows, followed by a domain and by a use case that gives no setting values.
then: Expects no `pattern-setting-missing`, and both rules owed.

title: A proof-only obligation counts as designed and built, has no satisfies gap and is never unsatisfied
when: No component satisfies any pattern rule.
then: Expects designed and built equal to the total in every domain, no `satisfies` gaps and no `unsatisfied` warnings.

title: Proved, planned and proof gaps of a proof-only obligation work as before
when: A domain's only test of two pattern rules is planned.
then: Expects both planned, both `proves` gaps, and `unproved` warnings saying the test is only planned.

title: A product cannot make pattern rules full obligations again: pattern_rule is Lathe's kind, so it is never widened
when: A product declares a kind named `pattern_rule`.
then: Expects the store to refuse it as a table name Lathe already has, and pattern rules to count as designed and built in each domain that owes them, with no `unsatisfied` or `unproved` warning.

title: A product's own proof-only kind is counted for proof alone, and a kind that is not an obligation is not counted
when: A product's own kind with `obligation` `proof` is proved by a test and satisfied by nothing.
then: Expects it designed, built and proved, with no warnings, and a `maybe` kind not counted at all.

title: A use case that follows a pattern needs no requirements of its own
when: Several use cases that follow patterns have no requirements.
then: Expects `use-case-without-requirements` only for the one that follows nothing.

title: An interaction requirement and a flow step may fulfill a pattern rule
then: Expects `fulfills` rules from `interaction_requirement` and `flow_step` to `pattern_rule`, and no `relation-not-allowed` for records that use them.

title: A step may fulfill the rules of the patterns its flow's use cases or its domain follow, and interaction requirements that fulfill them
when: Steps fulfill a rule of the domain's pattern, a rule of the use case's pattern, and an interaction requirement that fulfills one.
then: Expects none reported.

title: A step that fulfills a rule of a pattern only another use case follows is reported, as is an interaction requirement that fulfills it
then: Expects `flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow` for a step fulfilling a rule of a pattern only another use case follows, and for one fulfilling an interaction requirement that fulfills that rule, naming the flow's use cases.

title: The Tool Library still reads sensibly: its proof-only pattern rules are proved, with nothing asked for design
when: Loads this repo.
then: Expects TL-LEND to owe both Librarian action rules, all designed, built and proved, with no problem on the pattern's records.

title: A proved obligation that a planned test is also meant to prove is named, with that test
then: Expects `proof-still-owed` on two requirements proved by an automated and a manual test, each naming the planned test beside them, and none on a requirement no planned test is meant to prove.

title: A pattern rule owes proof only in the domain whose own planned test is meant to prove it
then: Expects `proof-still-owed` on a pattern rule in the domain whose planned test is meant to prove it, naming that domain, and not in the other following domain.

title: An obligation not yet proved, whose test is only planned, is unproved rather than proof-still-owed
then: Expects a requirement with only a planned test to get `unproved` and no `proof-still-owed`.

title: proof-still-owed names exactly the obligations planned_any counts beyond planned, in every fixture
when: Loads several fixtures.
then: Expects the obligations `proof-still-owed` names, per domain for pattern rules, to number exactly `planned_any` less `planned` summed over coverage.

title: A test proving only a rule of a pattern nobody follows is reported
then: Expects `proof-counts-nowhere` on a test that proves only a rule of a pattern no use case follows, saying so.

title: A test proving a pattern rule only another domain owes is reported; one in a domain that follows the pattern itself is not
then: Expects `proof-counts-nowhere` on a test in one domain proving a rule only another domain owes, naming both domains, and none on a test in a domain that follows the pattern itself.

title: Each target is named with its reason, and a planned test is judged too
then: Expects one message naming a record that is not an obligation and a rule outside every domain, each with its reason, and the warning on a planned test too.

title: A test proving a rule that every following use case marks not applicable is reported
then: Expects `proof-counts-nowhere` on a test proving a rule whose setting its only following use case gives a not-applicable reason.

title: A test with at least one proof that counts is not reported
then: Expects no `proof-counts-nowhere` on a test that proves one counted requirement beside a rule counted nowhere, and exactly the expected tests reported.

title: A manual test whose file names neither its ID, nor an ID it proves, nor its key is reported
then: Expects `manual-test-file-silent` on a manual test whose file is silent, and on one with a key the file lacks, naming the key.

title: A file naming the test, an ID it proves or its key is enough, and only manual tests are judged
then: Expects no warning for manual tests whose file names the test, an ID it proves, or its key, nor for a planned test sharing a silent file.

title: A test supports any obligation kind, with no role, labeled Supports and Supported by
then: Expects four `supports` rules, from a test to each obligation kind, each with no role and the labels Supports and Supported by, and no `relation-not-allowed` problem.

title: Support never counts as proof, automated or planned
then: Expects a requirement that an automated check only supports to stay unproved, and a planned check that supports a proved requirement to count in neither `planned` nor `planned_any`, and to raise no `proof-still-owed`.

title: A test that only supports owes no ID in its file, but its file must still exist
then: Expects no problem for an automated check that supports a requirement through a file naming no ID and with no key, nor for a planned one, and a `test-file-missing` error for a check whose `file` does not exist.

title: With a key_file, the key is looked for in that file, and a key it lacks is test-file-missing-id
then: Expects a test whose `file` never names its key, but whose key file does, to prove its domain rule with no problem, and a `test-file-missing-id` error naming the key file for a key the key file lacks.

title: A key file that is missing or outside the root is test-file-missing alone; for a planned test a missing one is a warning
then: Expects one `test-file-missing` error for a missing key file and one for a key file outside the root, a warning for a planned test's missing key file, no other problem on those tests, and the rule they claim to stay unproved.

title: With a key_file and no key, the proved IDs are looked for in the key file
then: Expects a test with a key file and no key to prove the domain rule the key file names, with no problem, and every proof-file problem in the fixture to come from the one test whose key the key file lacks.

title: The product page shows each domain as a card with its coverage bars and counts
when: Opens a product with two domains.
then: Checks one card per domain, linking to the domain page, with requirement and rule bars drawn to their share and labeled with their counts.

title: Coverage shows designed, built and proved on the product and domain pages
then: Checks the designed, built and proved counts of each domain on the product page's cards and on the domain page, a count of zero included.

title: The product page lists its open questions with owners, and its problems
then: Checks that the product page lists the product's open questions with their owners and what they are about, and only that product's problems, errors first.

title: The product page sums up the product's coverage, open questions and problems
when: Opens a product.
then: Checks its Summary's designed, built and proved totals, its open questions, errors and warnings; then opens a product with no obligations and checks its counts are zero.

title: Trace mode shows what fulfills, satisfies and proves a requirement, and its files
then: Expects the trace chain of a requirement to hold its view, component and test, the component implementing the view, and the two files they name, and nothing else.

title: Trace mode is offered only for requirements and domain rules
then: Expects trace mode to be available for a requirement and a domain rule and for no other kind.

title: The trace switch shows only the chain for a requirement and is absent for a use case
when: Switches on trace mode for a requirement.
then: Expects the file nodes to appear and the parent use case to go; Escape leaves trace mode; on a use case there is no switch.

title: Coverage shows one group per obligation kind with designed, built, proved and planned
when: Serves a workspace whose coverage has four obligation kinds, one of them a product's own.
then: Expects four labeled groups in the engine's order on the domain card and the domain page, each with designed, built, proved and planned, and a planned bar that is never drawn full.

title: The summary counts every obligation kind, and planned apart from proved
then: Expects the Summary's designed, built and proved totals over all four obligation kinds and a separate Planned line.

title: The domain page lists interaction requirements under their view, endpoint or flow
then: Expects interaction requirements nested under their view and endpoint, a product's own obligation kind nested under the endpoint, gap badges on their rows, nothing left under "Other records", and a search that keeps the endpoint above the matching interaction requirement.

title: The domain page tags each test with its state, and a planned test looks unfinished
then: Expects the tags automated (for a test with no state), manual and planned, and only the planned test's row and tag marked planned, with a title saying it does not count as proof.

title: The record page shows a test's state, and says a planned test is not proof
when: Opens a planned, a manual and an automated test.
then: Expects a State row with each state, the raw `state` field not repeated, and a note on the planned test only.

title: The record page shows where an interaction requirement sits and what it fulfills
